Overall, it did a good job on blending a keto powder. You start it upside down and flip it upright while the blades are moving. It was easy to clean as well...I just rinsed the jar with water, filled it about 1/3 full of water and blended again to clean the very-sharp blades, then rinsed the jar again.

I don't really care for the heavy glass jar. Since this hand blender needs flipped upside down and back, it makes it awkward. I have some arthritis in my hands, so I guess that makes it a little harder than if I had gym-worthy strong hands!

title: I LOVE My Pink Pop Babies, But This One Is Not Quite As Nice In Some Ways
text:
I have a little pink Pop Babies. I love it and use it daily. Then I saw this one which is supposed to be easier to clean and figured it would be a good backup. Let's see what happened.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This set comes with a pastel mint green Pop Babies. It has a thick clear plastic container, a twist on cap which has a rubberized ring on it, some nice blades, and a bottom that comes off the container for cleaning. The base is also separate.

HOW LONG TO CHARGE?
This takes only a couple of hours to charge up for me. I get about 15 or more times using it before I have to recharge.

HOW DOES IT WORK?
This works very well but it is smaller than the other one by 2 oz. When you are talking this size blender, 2 oz can mean a lot of action space. If you shake it from side to side while blending, it really does work nicely.

WHAT ELSE COMES WITH IT?
Tiny ice cube trays and a funnel come with this as well as a recipe booklet.

ANY PROBLEMS?
There is one problem I have- the top on this has a tendency to splash when I try to take it off- as in all over the place. The other unit NEVER does that.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I like the new green Pop Babies blender. It is very portable, gets quite a bit of action out of a charge, but the new design is not nearly as nice as the old one in that it sprays out when I open it. The blender works well other than that, although it is 2 oz smaller than the previous one, which I still prefer most of the time.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. The new top being a bit too much with the spray when I remove it and the smaller container made me take a star off. Otherwise it is a nice little blender which I like and will use alternately with the pink one which I love.

title: Not As Good Of A Set Up As Expected But It Works
text:
I have a cordless portable blender that i love, but it is getting older, so I thought a glass backup might be a good idea. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
BLADES
The blades of this are more than any other cordless portable blender I have tried out. There are SIX of them. That means that you can put in small chunks of fruit etc in the blender and it will work better than those with only four blades.

TOP
The top comes in two pieces. There is a top that screws on the glass container that has long narrow slits in it in the shape reminiscent of a daisy. These allow liquid to come through. The top that screws onto that is solid and has a rope handle on it like a carry strap. There is a plastic clear type of ring around the inside to keep contents from coming out.

GLASS CONTAINER
This container is very thick. The top and the bottom have different threads on it so that you don't accidentally put the wrong cover on the wrong end.

BASE
The base runs for 20 seconds. The digital readout has the charging information on it to let you know when it is charging and when it is full. It also reads out the seconds that you will be blending for.

EXTRA CARRY BASE
When you want to bring this container with you, or perhaps put it in the fridge, there is an additional base that comes with this that you can use to unscrew the base and screw the cover on making it more portable.

INSTRUCTIONS
The instructions for this are okay, but a little more explanation of parts and how to use them would make it better.

DOES IT WORK?
This blender does work. It not only blends chunks well, but is does break them into pretty good pulverized pieces. I don't recommend lots of hard things, however. The glass is nice, but you have to be smart about this. A little ice with the liquid and fruit is okay, but this is not an ice crusher by any means.

HOW TO USE
When using this blender, it is important to understand the concept in this blender. Not only do you blend the contents, but you have to shake it back and forth a few times gently and gradually during the 20 seconds that it is blending. That allows the contents to move around the container.

CHARGING
This only took a few hours to get to a full charge. I got quite a few uses before I had to recharge- 6-7 uses at least, but depending on what you are making and how many times you blend in a session.

THE BOTTOM LINE
IF you prefer a glass blender, this is a nice alternative to the usual plastic components found in this type of blender. It works well, and it is designed okay, but is a bit more cumbersome to use than other blenders. All said and done, being glass, this is well designed and I like it.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. It is not as easy to clean and assemble as my other blender, but it is glass, and it does work very well for what it is. I am concerned about the rubber rings, however, once these wear out and leak. There needs to be a set of rings offered for replacement in the future.

title: My New Favorite Smoothie Maker
text:
When it comes to travel, sometimes one of my kids or I find ourselves in need of a quick bite to eat, but we don't have the money or there is not anything fresh available. Enter the Pop Babies blender.

WHAT IS THIS BLENDER LIKE?
This blender is really cute. I have the pink one. It has four small blades in the top unit which screws off of the bottom where the motor is. There is a front button with a blue light around it. That shows when the item is charging when it is not full- it turns red. The top screws on with a little handle, allowing me to carry it if desired. There is a cord for USB charging that you need to plug into a USB power supply to charge it.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
I usually use juice, a soft banana broken into 1 inch pieces or so, a small handful of berries and make sure it is not more than 2/3 full of liquid. The cycle of blending lasts only for 20 seconds, and once or twice in a cycle, I gently shake the unit to re-distribute the fruit pieces . Usually two repetitions is enough to grind up the fruit.

HOW IS THE SMOOTHIE?
I find that adding powders is a bit harder to get to blend (spots will stick) but when using the fruit it seems to really do a great job of blending. I love this thing. It is so handy to bring in my backpack and put a few pieces of fruit and a packet of juice in with it. When it is time for the smoothie, I am good to go! I can even just pick up a couple of pieces of fruit at the store if needed.

HOW IS BATTERY LIFE?
I have used this 10 times this week and it is still going.

CLEAN UP?
Cleaning up is great. This comes with a funnel and a cleaning brush that is perfect for cleaning the container.

HOW MUCH DO YOU GET?
I fill up a smoothie glass that I usually would fill from a full sized blender only once, but it is just enough for me.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a great convenient way to make a smoothie on the go, this is wonderful. It does a great job of blending as long as you gently shake it a bit now and then to get the fruit all blended well.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is wonderful to take with me especially when doing artwork in the field or even to study with. Our kids will take it when they have to have an extended stay somewhere during the day and can not find a decent place to get a quick smoothie to drink. I think we will end up with some more of these for each of us in the future.

text:
The Hamilton Beach Mini Cordless Portable Personal Blender in Blue (51182) is a disappointment. The 6 Stainless Steel Blades can't even handle room-temperature bananas, let alone partially thawed fruit, so don't bother with ice at all. I did some research on replacement parts, because my daughter asked if there was an extra 16 oz. Blending Jar available. While the Hamilton Beach website has replacement Leakproof Travel Lids available, there is no chance of finding a spare blending jar; even a few internet searches didn't reveal one despite the fact that the jar will probably be the first part to fail since the plastic feels cheap. The USB Rechargeable battery seems to be the best part about this blender; it holds a charge well while being stored and the waterproof seal over the charging port makes the blender portion easy to clean; that is the only positive this blender has going for it.

The Bottom Line: Save your $32.99 and invest in a more powerful blender with extra portable cups.

title: Great for basic smoothie, not with frozen food
text:
I love my Nutri-bullet, but that is not something I travel with, so I'm so happy I found this! I have yet to try and take it through TSA (guessing it would get tossed given the blades, so not going to try it), but will take on road trips.

I blended a banana, protein powder, milk and flax seed and it worked great. The issue comes when adding in frozen items. While it blends, it does not break down the items well and I don't want to drink chunks of frozen spinach. That being said it is not a Nutri-Bullet and one should not expect high quality blender outcomes on a lower priced item. It works and does break them down some, but not to a smooth consistency like quality blenders. For the price it works well.

Now for the safety - I was concerned given the blades are attached to the bottom and what would happen if the "on" button was pressed without the cup securely in place. It has a built in safety feature so the blades will not turn on until the cup is secure with the arrow lined up to the "on" button. Obviously still need to be careful washing it (hand wash only for the base) but happy to know my finger wont get sliced off.

My only other concern would be that I'll be mid-blend and it will run out of battery., Love that it's USB chargeable, so need to make sure it stays charged. I likely wont let it go below 50% battery since I haven't yet figured out what % it takes for each use. I wish it had a battery icon instead of making us count lights.

title: This is great for making cat food smoothies
text:
I care for several geriatric and persnickety cats who loves to lick all of the gravy and leave all of the solids in their canned cat food. It dawned on me that these small blenders might be able to produce wet food at a consistency that would entice the cats to eat everything.

This blender easily handled various types of canned food and produced consistently evenly blended milkshake consistency food. The feline diners took a day or two to fully accept their new "smoothies", but now everything is polished off. This blender doesn't have dishwasher approved parts, so I use the hottest water possible to wash and then air dry every time I use it. It has only three separate parts: screw on lid, sturdy plastic open ended container and the base/blades/blending apparatus. It charges well, and I can get 3 or 4 blends in it before it requires recharging. It has just one speed, and it can be shut off at any point so that any solids that escaped the blades can be pushed down to be captured.

I'm pleased with the operation (simple and mostly idiot proof) and the product.

title: Overall a pretty useful product!
text:
I received this as a gift and it is really pretty good. The portable blender comes in handy for mixing my protein shakes and I've been adding bananas and peanut-butter to my shakes latetly too.
Just to set expectations: this is a portable, battery-powered blender, so it is not going to have the full power of a full-size, plug-in blender; but it is really quite powerful enough. I've had a few times where it will generate an error message that it can't blend upon startup because the contents are too hard or viscous, but I just shake the bottle or tip it upside-down while it starts up and then set it down on the counter after a second once the blades get going and then it has no problem continuing.
When you press the button, the blender will run for 20-seconds continuous (counting up on the LED) and then shut off by itself. So you can hit the button, place it on the counter, and anytime after 20 seconds, pick up your drink.
The battery seems good, able to run many blends before needing a recharge, and it's a standard charging cable so I have the cables everywhere already for all different devices, which is handy.
The weird thing about it is the flap that covers the charging port. It just kind of hangs there and if you try to push it up on there so it 'sticks' in there, it just comes out and dangles loosely again. I put a piece of tape over it to hold it on there in between charging sessions, but then the motor gets an error probably due to potential overheat because I then noticed that the unit has no vents at all on it. This I actually like because when I rinse the blades, I don't have to worry about water getting in to the electronics and motor area. I just hold the charging port cover over the USB ports when I rinse it and it appears that completely seals it up protecting it from water.
There's the mini-USB charging port (I think that's what it's called) and then there's a regular USB port to. I received mine at Christmas, so I may have lost the directions in the shuffle of everything, but I really am not sure what the regular USB is for. I tried to charge it in there and plug things in but nothing happens, so that must be where the manufacturer programs the unit.
The size is OK, but I wish I had gotten the larger one.
The strength is good - crushing everything that I've needed to do. If it hiccups at first, I just flip it upside-down for a minute so the blades aren't contacting the liquid and once they get up to speed after a sec it has no problem.
I can make the shake at night, put the whole thing in the fridge including the motor, take it out in the AM and give it a quick re-stir and it's golden.
I like how it's totally portable - it really gives some freedom on where you can go.
I'll just do powder sometimes and no fruit and it makes the powder absorb better than a blender bottle.
Overall a pretty good product!

title: Neat portable blender
text:
[[VIDEOID:4ec7a6b8819f36827a37a170aca26431]] This is a neat blender, but you have to know it's limitations. By limitations, don't expect it to work as a normal blender because it runs off the battery. If the battery doesn't have sufficient charge, you won't be able to blend with it. The included manual doesn't mention if you can use it while it's charging, but it's probably a good assumption that it takes more power to run that blender motor than what's being put into the battery to charge it. Anyways, charge the battery up before you plan to use it.

It is a nice blender that comes with a bottom lid so you can use the blender container as a drink container. The top lid has a flip top so you can drink from it as a drink container, and also includes a nice carrying strap.

When you twist the blender container off/on the blender base, LED lights light up. Green means that the container is secured on the base and is ready to be used as a blender. Red means that the container isn't ready to be used as a blender.

The LEDs are also used as charging indicators when you plug in the included charging cable to charge the blender battery. Only a charging cable is included and NOT a power adapter/brick. Luckily I had an extra power adapter from one of my old phones lying around, and I used it to charge the blender battery. If the battery is not fully charged, you'll see red LEDs around the top of the blender base. As the battery gets charged, the red LEDs turn green. When all LEDs are green, then the blender is fully charged.

The LEDs also light up when you are actually running the blender. The blender has 2 modes. One mode just runs the blender non-stop when you start it, and ends when you stop it. The other mode is a pulse mode. All of this is controlled via the single front power button on the blender base.

Cleaning the lids and container is easy with just soap and water. You can wash the blender base, but the manual says to not submerge under water (since it houses the battery). I washed the blender base by holding only the blades under running water and gently sponge the blades and top portion of the base with soap.

The blades are not removeable, and neither is the battery. The ad says the blades are SUS 304, which is a food safe, corrosion resistant stainless steel used in food appliances, utensils, and food storage.

Since the blender is new, everything runs fine and the battery is strong. My concern is what happens down the road when the battery no longer holds a full charge. It'll be a shame to toss it, when maybe a set of fresh rechargeable batteries might do the trick.

Anyways, I'll have to update my review when that day comes.

Overall, it's a great blender to make smoothies or to even use as a food processor when you're out and about or camping.

title: Portable but small personal blender--great for fruit, vegetables but maybe not big ice chunks
text:
This review is for TIKBABA's portable personal blender. Let me start by saying that I bought this to bring on a cruise ship where smoothies aren't readily available but I don't want the same breakfast buffet day after day. I think this will work great in that type of environment where you have a range of fruit and available milk, ice cream, and small ice cubes to whip something up. The blender is really lightweight and fairly small, and you can use the hot water to rinse it out and reuse it.

Take this to a home's kitchen, and I'm finding it more difficult to justify rather than just a fullsize blender that you can get at a cheaper price at a Walmart or Target. The blender is personal size, but it didn't fill an 8oz cup. You're going to be making several smoothies at a time if you intend for it to make something that compares to any smoothie or juice restaurant. The blades appear to be well made, but it took a lot of use to get them to actually chop up my thicker refrigerator ice. They worked really well on smaller ice cubes---you know, the "good ice" from certain chicken fast food chains. But, my refrigerator ice challenged this blender.

The device came charged so it was easy to use after a quick cleaning. I didn't have to track down batteries or wait for it to charge. The instructions are really simple and a quick read though it's fairly intuitive what you're meant to do with the different components.

title: Smaller than expected, works ok
text:
I bought this in hopes to use for my cleansing program, but was surprised when I opened it how small the container was. The seller doesn't really give any photos showing the size, which would be helpful. I did see it was listed as 320ml which is 12oz.(cup and a half) For reference a standard disposable water bottle is 16oz this can't even hold that. I ended up purchasing another one that holds 20oz so I can do my cleanse.

This one "kinda" works for my protein shakes that only need 1 cup of water (8oz) so I'll keep for that, as it just fits. Blending power is mediocre at best. First day I tried my protein shake, filled with water, then added protein powder on top. the blender wasn't powerful enough to mix and get to the powder on top! Made a mess trying to use a knife to scrape and readjust enough to get it smooth enough to drink. Found it works better to add powder first, then water, still sticks around the sides a bit, but gets the job done. Also really only has enough power on one full charge to do a blend, then you have to charge each time. So if you need for anything more than 1 cup water and 2 scoops protein powder, its too small. If it had a bit more room might blend better, but everything is so compacted in the small space, doesn't give enough room to move around and blend. When just doing liquid only ingredients it worked well, but didn't handle powders well.

I had to laugh at the recipes that were included, first one called for 2 bananas, 1/2 cup yogurt and a few other things.... this blender wouldn't even hold 1 banana, certainly not 2. I pictured with a standard Gatorade bottle so you get idea of size, as well as just the glass part next to a tall shot glass. Look how small the glass container part is! looks big overall with base and top but the part that actually holds what you want to blend is REALLY small. So if you need more than 1 cup of liquid, this isn't the blender for you. Works OK and love that I can recharge it, just really tiny! The top comes with two options, one has a strainer and the other is a solid screw cap. You can't drink out of it without removing the top, no flip top drink spout or anything. Figured I should mention that since their photos literally show the same thing twice and give no hint to what it can or can't do.

Overall, this blender is WAY too small, not terribly powerful if you are trying to actually fully blend anything powder based. I haven't tried with frozen fruit or ice, but can't imagine it can handle that well. I would say look elsewhere for one that is a bit larger to allow your ingredients to actually have room to move around and blend together. Seller would benefit from making this just a tad larger to work properly. Giving two stars as the recharge feature is nice, although doesn't hold charge very long and one touch start is nice - if it were big enough to work properly would give 5 stars.

title: A good light duty blender
text:
Assuming you are looking for a light duty portable blender, this might be the one. It has very basic operation: Blend or Pulse. It has a good safety interlock so the base knows when it is attached to the bottle and it's safe to activate the blade. The top almost seems complicated, but is well thought out. There is a loop for hanging, a loop that secures the flip top, and a release latch. Everything locks into place so nothing is dangling and destined to get broken. It is easy to clean, but use caution when cleaning the base, only washing the blade area, not submerging the whole thing.

I emphasis "light duty" because the directions are very clear on what is and isn't acceptable. Ice is a no. Fruit with thick skin is a no. Fruit and other solid items need to be cut into 1" chunks and they specifically say to add your "liquid" (vs ice). If you are good with that and need something portable, this is a great option.

title: Decent Design, Not Much Blending Power
text:
My wife and I make smoothies every day, and I'm on a quest for the perfect rechargeable portable blender. This is almost, but not quite it.

It is basically a nicely-made blender, and it has a 32 oz capacity, which is quite a bit larger than the typical "personal" blender. It comes with a travel cap and a strainer insert, along with something they call a "tray," a round disc that fits across the mouth of the bottle. There is no hint in the instruction book what the purpose of that tray might be.

Where it falls short is blending power. I tried to make a version of the smoothie I normally make in my countertop blender; I cut everything into very small pieced and eliminated some ingredients that might be harder than it is intended for. I was meticulous about the max lines and careful to follow the recommendations to hold it at a 45 degree angle and shake it while blending. The result is that I ran through the entire charge on the machine without finishing the smoothie - I ended up dumping the half-blended contents into my countertop blender to finish it off in about 20 seconds.

One thing I am really not crazy about is the magnetic charger, similar (maybe identical) to the one used in some inexpensive smart watches. I have lots of USB A, USB C, and Micro-USB cables lying around, and adding another cable type to keep track of is pretty inconvenient.

I feel like I will be able to make use of this blender while we are traveling by making a very much simplified smoothie recipe. In the meantime I will keep going on my quest.

title: Great Chopper, Great Blender
text:
This is not my first GREECHO product. I have a small personal blender from them that I use when I'm traveling and like very much, so I was eager to give this a try. It totally lived up to my expectations.

I would like to note up front that the capacity of all the cups provided is small, so you will either use this appliance for a small family (like mine - just the two of us) or you will be making multiple batches. This should come as no surprise, since it's advertised as a personal blender. Also, device is so quick and easy to use that multiple batches are not a problem.

In action this tool is fantastic. The first thing I did with it was make coleslaw with the chopper cup, and it worked perfectly. I tossed a few baby carrots in with the cabbage, and it all chopped and mixed it all into the best coleslaw I've had in a very long time. I'll say that when you are chopping something like this, you want to be careful. This could turn your cabbage into puree pretty quickly if you are too heavy on the button, so you just pulse it a second or two at a time until you get the chop you want.

Next I made a smoothie, which is the more common use this will get in our house. My trial smoothie consisted of half a banana, a small beet, beet juice, mango juice, kale, protein powder, dry oatmeal, coconut, and some frozen cherries. It was great.

I have not had a chance to use the grinder yet. It will probably come into play when I need some ground nuts for a future recipe, and I have no doubt that it will work just as well in that job. Highly recommended.

title: A Very Nice Travel Blender
text:
I got this to make my daily smoothies when I'm traveling. It isn't quite as powerful as the NutriBullet I use every day, but I never expected that it would be. It has a very small 340 ml capacity (a little less than a cup and a half), and they are serious about that maximum fill line. Overfill it (first thing I did) and it will jam.

Once you adjust your quantity expectations and your recipe, it works great. It's relatively quiet and effective. It even blended a lemon, peel and all (I suggest that you take out the seeds). It times-out at 40 seconds, which is more than enough time to get everything nicely blended.

It works on a standard USB-C charging cable, which is provided. There is no charger, which is fine by me - I think most people have plenty of those lying around. It's lightweight, but it feels substantial and well-made. Cleaning it is a matter of putting a little water in it and turning it on for a few seconds.

The battery seems to be really robust. I made four smoothies in a row on a single charge and it still had power left. It's the size of a standard water bottle or drink cup, so it drops right into a bag to transport and fits in the console of the car. There is a nice little rubber carrying strap, which I will likely never use, but even that seems to be high quality.

This is not a cheap blender, it feels like good quality for the money.

title: Nice Blender!
text:
I recently decided to start using meal replacement shakes for lunch. I've tried various little hand-held shaker-style bottles with the little blender inside, but couldn't really find one that I liked or that was powerful enough to blend ice.

I have to say that I'm more impressed with this version of the Blend-Jet-style blender, than others that I've tried before. Firstly, I like that I can detach the cup from the base & it has a cap for that bottom half to protect that area. Secondly, the lid is very user friendly, as it snaps shut to keep the contents from leaking out of it. And it's very sports bottle like. Thirdly, this is a pretty powerful blender & while I wouldn't recommend putting cube-like chunks of ice inside of it, it can certainly handle the kind of ice that comes out of your refrigerator.

I haven't tried blending frozen fruit or vegetables in it yet, but it certainly works for my meal replacement powders, milk, & ice. I get a smooth blend & this is truly small enough to be portable, but big enough to create a smoothie like drink to fill you up. I like it.

title: Good for occasional or travel use but won't replace your corded blender
text:
[[VIDEOID:420b9d0a281ea6bf0296349a009869d4]] We got this for making protein shakes, and it has worked for that, although not without some issues. First, it isn't as powerful as our corded countertop blender. This isn't a surprise, but it is noteworthy. We've cut down a bit on the frozen fruit added to the shake to allow for proper blending. Usually we blend fruit (frozen banana chunks and frozen strawberries), a liquid (normally cashew or other milk) and protein powder.

This unit will blend them, but it struggles just a bit. We find that shaking and rotating the unit a bit helps, but still it isn't a guarantee that full blending will result. However, it is working adequately for us.

What do we like? The cup is a decent size (some other rechargeable blenders have smaller blending containers.) We also like that you can remove the blades from the base and replace with a plain base, thereby converting it from a blending container to a drink container. Usually we have to transfer the blended contents to another glass. The lights clearly tell you the charge state and whether the base is properly attached to the blending container. It is fairly easy to clean (although the base can be tough to remove from the container sometimes.)

What do we not like as much? Another older unit we have will not power up unless both the base and the lid are properly attached. This one allow the motor to engage when the top was not securely attached. This could result in quite a mess! We understand that traditional blenders are similar in design, but they aren't intended to be held in one's hands while blending. It's not a deal breaker, though. Also the power is a bit lacking, but again it is portable, so on balance that isn't as bad as it would be with a corded blender.

If you are patient and don't fill this to the top it should perform satisfactorily, and you can take it on the road whereas a corded blender only goes as far as its cord will permit. So we recommend this blender as long as your expectations are properly adjusted. Don't expect full size corded blender performance, and do recall that this will operate literally anywhere, and you'll probably be happy with it as we are.

text:

That being said, I'm only rating it so highly because of how easy it is to clean.

Despite the container being a decent size, the fill line means that you're only getting about half of that for a drink. Any drink that you make is going to be a mini one, I'd say maybe a little over half of what most other personal blenders can make. The reason for this is because of the blades, I'm sure of it.

I've tried it three ways:
1. Filled to the fill line with frozen fruit and water. This blended decently well, but was thick.
2. Filled to the fill line with frozen fruit and a smoothie drink. Proceeded to spend the next twenty minutes trying to get it to blend.
3. Filled to the fill line with a smoothie drink and a small amount of frozen fruit. Blended well.

It can't seem to handle too many solid ingredients, and it's hard to identify what the hidden fill line will be for that. What most blenders can easily handle, this one can't. It's honestly astonishing for a Hamilton Beach product to be this subpar, I've had no-name products do far better.

Overall, I'd say skip this unless you're using it for a protein shake or something that isn't meant to be ice cold.

title: On The Heavy Side And Small, But Good Blending Power
text:
With so many rechargeable portable blenders out there, it can be tough to know which one to choose. They are all roughly the same price, but some are better than others.

What is Good About This Blender?

1. I like the glass cup. It sets this one apart from the others and makes it easier to clean. The plastic cups get scratched and marred over time and even stained from food and juice.

2. This blender is more powerful than my other one (see picture, the iOCSmart is on the right). The iOCSmart took less time to blend this morning's smoothie (raspberries, hazelnut milk, maca powder, vitamin C powder, protein powder), and amazingly, clumps of protein powder did not stick to the glass cup. Protein powder always sticks to the plastic cup.

3. It is easy to use. Just a one-button operation. Easy to charge too.

What Is Not So Great About This Blender?

1. Because of the glass cup, this blender is on the heavier side. You would think twice about throwing it in a backpack and carrying it around. For some, that might make it less "portable."

2. The glass cup is on the small side. It has less capacity than my other portable blender (see picture again). It will still provide enough for one serving, I just need to get used to it because I am used to having some leftover for later.

3. Cleaning - yes it is fairly easy to clean, however I have noticed that food or protein powder tends to stick to the area under the blades and around the base. That area is not as easy to clean. I had to roll up some paper towel and really squeeze it in there and around the base to get at the stuck protein powder.

Overall Would I Recommend This?

I would, because it seems well-made, sturdy, and it's fairly easy to use. It is also powerful for it's blender class. The only drawbacks are the small size, relative heaviness, and minor issues with the area under the blades. Overall I would rate this one 3.75 stars.

My other portable blender's battery seems to be dying which is why I tried this one. I have had that one for less than a year. Time will tell if the lithium polymer battery in the iOCSmart lasts longer than the one in my other blender.

Update 11.12.2021:
Well this blender's battery is dying too. I get maybe 2 - 3 uses out of it before I have to recharge it. I would have purchased another but the new model has a plastic cup and not glass. I'd like to find a similar device with a glass cup; so far I have not find one that has decent reviews.

title: Works great with the right ingredients
text:
This is such a great alternative to the other brands that cost so much more.
This kit comes with the bottle which holds so much, the blender unit, a bottom cap, top cap and a usb c cable for charging.
Before use I made sure to wash everything out and to charge the blender up with the included cable.
Once charged you place the blender on top the bottle and line up the arrow on the bottle to the blender switch.
Now you need to have certain expectations in check while using something this compact and low power. You can’t expect to have the power of a full sized blender. Don’t. This is a compact solution for on the go.
With that in mind, make sure to have enough liquid to blend otherwise it’ll jam up. Frozen fruits and ice will blend but you need to be patient and you need to work at it.
I placed frozen berries, ice cream and milk into the bottle. Now you can’t go straight into a full blend. You need to pulse it and good a good speed before getting into the pulse or blend. Once to speed you can allow your frozen fruit to hit the blades and it will blend! You can’t start with the fruit at the blades at a full stop. Get up to speed first.
But you can see the results! It totally blended the fruit and the everything else together.
After blending, you can just place the bottom cap if you don’t want to carry around the blender. It’ll look just like a regular bottle.
It’s nice that they included a charge indicator into the blender. You can see the charge by how many green lights there are as opposed to the red ones.
I do wish they included a usb c cover to use while washing but you can avoid that spot yourself. Overall, this product works as long as you know how to use it!

text:
The container part is dishwasher safe but the part with the blade cannot be put in the dishwasher and should be hand washed but the whole thing is easy to deal with. The contents were all blended smoothly.

Okay so first thing you have to know

When you first get it you may need to charge it for a couple of hours. It has a neat magnetic charger.
Once it’s charged the light will turn blue. You fill the tumbler and the. Screw on the cap. Be careful not to over fill. Once you turn it on you will hold the container upside down for best results. Once it’s blended you’ll see the button turn orange. It also turns orange if the battery is low or the cap is loose. It won’t turn on if it’s orange.

Once you remove the cap if your contents aren’t blended like you want, stir a bit and screw the cap back on and start the blender.

It’s pretty cool. Takes a minute and it blends a single serving smoothie or milkshake. I honestly cannot complain.

The only thing I don’t like is battery life. I got three blends before it needed charged again. I guess that’s fine but I don’t know why I just expected a better battery.

It’s worth the price though.

title: A bit of a learning curve and balancing act, but not bad
text:
I love to drink smoothies. They are refreshing and healthy and make for a great start to the day. My problem is I am not one who wakes up early enough in the mornings to easily pull this off. So I was intrigued by this portable blender with a USB port.

As long as I am to work on time in the morning, I can still make my breakfast and eat it right there, as long as no one is coming in. (And I rarely have people stopping in to see me.) I can premeasure the fruits that I want to use and store those in the freezer at work, or have them at home and grab a bag on my way out the door.

I have experimented with it several times now and have had a bit of a frustration factor trying to figure out the best amount of frozen fruits to put into it without overloading the blender. If it senses that something is too tough to cut through, it will not work, of course. And of course, fresh fruits work better.

The liquid factor is imperative. You absolutely need to have almost a ratio of 50% solids and 50% liquid to make this properly work.

What I really like: It is convenient to use and carry with you, except the funnel is a bit more awkward. But I love using the funnel so that I’m not chasing berries that rolled away when I was trying to get them in the top of the bottle.

It’s easy to charge by just plugging into your computer. The charge seems to last a decent amount of time at least a couple of days. I like to top it off periodically so that I’m not surprised by a lack of charge when I’m eager to get my smoothie ready.

You can drink right out of the bottle and not have to dirty up another glass.

It’s super easy to clean, actually. I usually rinse it out right away. I’ve even used the blending feature to whip up a drop of dishsoap with water inside. Sometimes if I add peanut butter, that may stick to the side, but I have a mini spatula that easily removes that. I also have some wand sponges that easily fit inside.

The blender comes with a great booklet that has 50 different juicing and blending recipes. I’m interested in trying some of them to complement the ones I make on my own.

What I didn’t like: It can be temperamental. It’s hard to tell if the battery is low. It’ll look like it is indicating it is ready to go, but then it stalls out and needs to be charged for a bit. This is why I try to top it off periodically. It also can be temperamental with what it wants to blend. I felt like what worked one day didn’t necessarily work the next day.

It comes with a silicone ice tray so that you can make mini ice cubes that are literally cubes. I was excited about this until I tried to use it. It was difficult to fill. And then when I was trying to pop out the ice cubes, most of them were stuck. Twisting the tray to release them caused them to pop out all over the place. So I don’t think I will be using that piece that often. But I really don’t need it.

So overall, I’m enjoying this little blender for the most part. I hope it holds up for a while.

text: I first tried this blender using crushed ice, almond milk, yogurt, and a pitted date cut in half. I expected it to be slushy when finished, but there were still pieces of crushed ice and the two pieces of date were untouched. The container also leaked.  I thought what am I doing wrong?  I guess everything. Make a smoothie part 2.  I again used crushed ice, some almond milk, one date cut in half, and water. There is a little arrow pointing down at the bottom of the plastic container. It MUST be aligned exactly with the black marker below the start button. If not aligned, the container will leak. If aligned, the container does not leak.  When the blender was mixing, I tilted it back and forth several times as shown in the ad. This seems to be the trick as the crushed ice turned into slush, and the date blended into the mix.  One part I still do not understand is the ad shows that you can immerse the entire container in water without damage.  On the instructions in the box (see picture) it states, "It is prohibited to soak the base in water or put it into the dishwasher for cleaning to avoid damage to the battery after water inside." What does this mean? Can or can not the entire blender be put in water? It also shows in the ad a woman who puts a container filled with a smoothie sideways into her bag. I would not be brave enough to do this unless the bag was ready for the garbage anyway. Considering the flop I made of a smoothie the first time around, the second try was a success. I do think this is a good single-serve blender if done correctly.  As for immersing it in water, I will not be doing this for the base. title: Ultra Portable, Easy to use - Be REALLY careful when cleaning and drying it! -- Updated
text:
[[VIDEOID:d26bef5926fdcc19a328c94870889f23]] Overall I would give this blender a 3 -3.5 star rating. It is super portable per the description and seems like it would hold a charge long enough to make a few smoothies depending on how hard you make it work.

Do you use frozen fruit? Ice? Or just some Almond milk and fresh fruit? The instructions did not say anything about ice or frozen fruit.

As mentioned the blender is pretty portable and would work nicely for a quick blend at the office or in a motorhome where we will probably use it most as we travel. It's USB rechargeable so you can charge it off of a plug or through the computer which is what we did and it's super easy to operate with one button control.

The reason for the lower rating is that first and foremost it is difficult to clean! You can't separate the base from the container so it would be difficult to get any leftover pieces of fruit out if they did not come out with a pour. You can't get the base wet so we put some soap and water in the container and then turned the blender on which worked for us but then it's really difficult to dry the inside. You don't want to go sticking your fingers in there without being absolutely sure that you won't accidentally turn it on and blend your fingers. We put a couple of paper towels in it then let it air dry. (we did accidentally turn it on a couple of times while normally handling it)

Not too sure if you should be using ice or frozen fruit? That's all we had and it did leave chunks of ice and fruit but they were not super big pieces but a couple of them were about the size of a dime. Maybe it would be better with fresh fruit and a liquid of your choosing.

UPDATE: Bump to 4 stars and you can clean it a little easier.

We did some more testing and research on this and you CAN remove the container from the base. When we originally tested it the two parts would not move and we didn't want to break it so we didn't force it. After seeing some other videos and reviews we tried to remove the two parts and they came out.

So since we are able to do that some of our original dislikes on this are null and void. It is easier to clean than we thought but the base with the blade still may be difficult to clean and you should be a little more cautious when cleaning not to hit the power button with the base off.

We still don't think that it's really meant for frozen fruit and ice as it did leave some chunks even after shaking it around during the blending process.

We will for sure try this out some more in our RV during our next road trip.

Thanks!

text:
Every year in January I start the inevitable diet that is necessary after a month of holiday dinners and treats. I've already bought a jar of vanilla protein powder and 1 of chocolate so with this blender, I will not have one excuse to put it off on January 1st. Well maybe January 2nd...

Anyway the plastic jar on this cute little blender looks small but it holds 16 ounces - perfect for a protein shake. I love that it's cordless. There is a small jar that protects the blade when not in use and doubles as a measuring cup. And when you're done with your shake or smoothie, just add water and soap to the jar and blend it up, rinse out the canister, rinse the blades and your done. Sometimes the protein powder gets gummy around the bottom of the blender so you may need to use the tip of a knife (carefully) to get that loose.

I don't need my shakes to be thick so I haven't experimented with ice or frozen fruit so I will leave that to others to review. I do like it to be cold so I often put the milk and whatever fresh fruit I have in the freezer for awhile before I blend it. It does take a couple of times to get the powder to mix completely though, but that's only about a minute so can't complain about that. Thick chunks of banana didn't cause a problem nor did the peanut butter I added to one chocolate shake.

I plugged it in to recharge when I first got it out of the box and it was fully charged in less than 2 hours. I've used it a few times since just to check it out and it's still showing fully charged. (You can check by pressing and holding the power button for 3 seconds - first it will flash red to show that it's in battery level mode - then it will show blue for fully charged or alternate blue/red that it's 50% charged or red which means it need a recharge.

It's powerful enough to mix my protein shakes, it's portable with a lid if you need to take it with you on the go, it can be easily cleaned and stored away until next time and there's even recipes in the back of the instruction booklet...what's not to like?

title: Great portable blender but the specs are wrong
text:
One of the pictures, in the seller's description, says the blades move at 24,000 rpm. Then the number of speeds listed is 26,000 (which is also stated in the first paragraph of the text description). But the manual that comes with it says "motor speed 18,000 rpm".

I don't like that! While it doesn't really matter that much in real life, the contradiction in numbers makes me question the product. Or, at least, the seller's understanding of the product.

That said: it's plenty fast and powerful. I made a smoothie using frozen fruit this morning and it worked perfectly. I like the capacity (about 40% larger than my other portable blender). And I like the multi-use lights at the base. They look nice and the number of them turning on denotes the battery charge.

It's a very solid device. I would rate it higher, on those merits alone, but giving the wrong specs doesn't fill me with confidence.

Or maybe I'm just reading the specs wrong.

title: Gimmie more blender bottles.
text:
I’m currently obsessed with blender bottles. I love smoothies, milkshakes, protein shakes, but it can be hard to make those items without dirtying up your big blender. In comes personal sized blenders. You can literally almost do everything with this smaller blender that you can with the big one and it’s MUCH less dirty.

No matter your health goals, how many people are in your family, it doesn’t matter. These are perfect for anyone and everyone. These make the perfect gift for anyone or for yourself. When you get your blender it does come inside of a box that does tell you exactly what is inside. I would recommend wrapping to keep big the surprise going a little more.

Inside the box is:

(1) Blender
(1) Bottom cap
(1) Cup brush
(1) Silicone brush
(1) Silicone Straw
(1) Charging Cables
(1) Users Manuel

You get quite a few items with this blender. I would highly recommend reading the users manual before you try and use your blender, just so you have a better understanding of your new blender.

This a very powerful blender! As soon as I got it. I made a fruit smoothie and it worked perfectly. I followed the directions and added fruit and water up until the max fill line. I did blend it for 30 second like recommend but mines didn’t completely blend up but that’s MY FAULT! I added too much fruit and not enough liquid, once I added a little more water. I was able to shake it. Shaking it is something that’s recommended to help move the items in the blender around. You can blend your items or you can pulse. This blender will blend for 30 seconds straight but will automatically turn off after 30 seconds.

Once I corrected my water situation. It blended my pineapples and strawberries beautifully. I wouldn’t say this is super loud. If people are home, they will hear it. Even when using it when the tv on. Now if you have music blasting, no you won’t hear it. It is completely water proof so you don’t have to worry about dripping and spilling. Now, if you over fill the cup. You can and will cause spilling. Over filling it will also cause the blades to not spend properly which means you will spend more time trying to blend one smoothie. The body of the blender can be used as a blender cup. You can just detach it. Put on the extra cap that came with it and you will be set.

Washing this personal blender is very easy. You can pretty much take all the pieces apart which allows you to properly clean. You don’t have to worry about leaving behind parts of food or clumps of protein powder. Even through its waterproof. I don’t recommend putting items like this in the dishwasher. You should always wash items like this out by hand.
When I got mines, I did charge it for 4 hours like recommend. I’ve used it 3 times in the last 48 hours and it shows no sign of needing to be recharged anytime soon. I’m unsure how long a charge will last so I plan to charge it every Sunday so that it’s ready for the week.

text:
[[VIDEOID:6caf4f399ce1f2c799c3d270512a9b61]] Worse device EVER CREATED! The good reviews that I see on here all seem to be for the glass version but with 2 kids glass is not ideal for me, so I got the titan version. It's the worst!!! This is getting sent back immediately! There's nothing worse than being hungry and having to fight with a leaky, faulty, frustrating device for 45 minutes just to end up with strawberry milk.
Let me explain...
I recieved this device about a week late, plugged it in and read both booklets while it was charging. I waited until the light was white to indicate it was fully charged before using. I cleaned it thouroughly before use and was excited to try my new personal blender.
I added 5 frozen blueberries, 2 frozen strawberries (small and cut in half), a table spoon of yogurt, about 4oz of milk and 1/2 scoop of ladyboss lean powder. I push and hold the button to start and... bzzzzztt.... blender does about 1/2 a second pulse then stops... I check to see what the flashing lights indicate as there are troubleshooting instructions in the manual, for example flashes between red and white 10 times means motor is locked up.
Lights flashed 3 times between red and white... unfortunately there is no instruction to tell me what this means.
I thought maybe there was too much in the machine as it specifies only fill 2/3 of the way.
So I dump a little out and try again... same thing... I try adding milk thinking the food to liquid ratio is off as there is mention of this in troubleshooting. Same problem... I do this 3 more times until the blender is less than1/2 way full and is about 80% milk with only 1/2 of a strawberry and some blueberry shreds left in my recipe. FINALLY it turns on and runs for 34 seconds (yes I timed it, I was that annoyed by this point.) When it finished I dumped it into a cup so I could try to blend the remaining ingredients that I had dumped into a seperate cup during trial and error. I had the same issue... by the time i was finished i ended up throwing the whole smoothie away because it tasted like luke warm berry flavored milk froth because I had to add SO MUCH more liquid and it took 45 minutes to make it work. This device is the absolute worse... I ordered this at the end of March and expected it by March 30th. The expected date had changed to April 1st and I swear feel like this was a sick April fools joke. I do not like using the word hate, but I hate this thing SO MUCH!

title: Pretty Good, Would serve most people well.
text:
Doing daily protein shakes and got sick of the stinky plastic/stainless bottles so I looked into a glass personal blender. This does not work how I thought, however it does the job well enough.m for the price (~$30USD)

From photos, I interpreted that the bottom cap sat in the base and the blades stayed inside the unit while consuming. After blending, you need to either flip the unit and put on a 2nd supplied cap, or keep the bulkier motor assembly on the bottle. If you want something slimline and portable you’ll be leaving the dirty blades and motor on your kitchen counter until you can return the bottle to the unit w/ some soap. I’d love to see them sell the bottle separately so you could always clean everything promptly.

The top of the container screws on tightly most times, but every once in a while the threads will slip (not over torquing) so just keep turning and it will lock down eventually.

Tried ice (cubed and crushed from the fridge) and it made a fine snow-cone like fluff at the bottom that congealed without chopping up the rest of the larger pieces. When adding water it became no better and formed an ice doughnut on the bottom of the unit with I chopped ice on top. I’d probably pass on more than a cube or two but the motor can handle it. Very powerful unit.

It’s a great safety feature that the unit will not run w/o the jar attached and the button must be pressed twice to activate the unit. Cleaning is a breeze as expected. Just run with a tiny dab of soap and warm water.

If you’re doing protein powder and maybe some fruit it should do very well and not get stinky. Maybe an ice cube or three after the first mix at most. Additionally it can handle warm beverages like coffee and tea (no super hot liquids) which seems specific to this unit.

title: Works well for most things, appreciate the glass container
text:
[[VIDEOID:c1e5c7b1638bc2bb98b16608433499cf]] This is the first personal size blender I've ever used. It works pretty good.

The Good:
- I like that this personal blender has a glass container versus plastic. - The container is 10-ounces, so a good size for a smoothie. It also looks a lot like a beverage glass, and is easy to drink out of. I like that.
- The blender glass is very easy to clean.
- The bottom of the blender has a rubber pad that helps keep it from moving on the counter while blending.

The Bad:
- Doesn't come with the USB adapter - just the USB cable.
- Doesn't chop frozen fruit very well if the fruit is 1-inch pieces - such as frozen pineapple chunks. It will chop frozen blueberries easily, but it struggles with pieces that are larger.
- If the blender can't chop whatever is in there, it will stop and the red light appears. You have to either remove the glass and scrape down the sides of the glass, or you have to shake the glass to get the contents to move. Pulsing the blender does not help.
- The base of the blender is a little tricky to clean. When you remove the glass, some of the contents might drip into the rim around the blades, so you have to rinse that out carefully without getting the base wet.

The Workaround:
- If using frozen fruit, allow the fruit to slightly thaw before blending. This isn't an ideal workaround when you're running short on time, but it will help.
- Gently shake the blender and tip it upside down and then right side up again while it's turned on. This helps to move the contents of the blender around for more even blending.
- Put frozen fruit or chunky things into the glass first, then add the rest of your smooth ingredients (such as ice cream, yogurt, milk, etc.). By doing this, the blender will blend the smooth things first and the chunkier bits will eventually fall down and get blended - you will have to shake the blender a little to help move those chunky bits down. IF you put the soft items in first, and end with the chunky bits, the blades hit those larger bits first and it has a harder time blending without shutting off.

If you turn on the blender and leave it run while sitting on the counter, it turns itself off after a period of time.

Overall, I do think this is a nice blender and it will continue to get used in our house.

title: Be aware of its limitations
text:
Build quality is better than expected and it arrived well packaged. But it has a LOT of instructions about what NOT to do. So I find washing this too much of a PITA. Am I lazy? First world problem? Oh yes. And that’s on me. But because of the external charging port, I’m awfully paranoid about getting it wet; the various warnings did their job I guess. I’m a total mess when making drinks, and even though this port is on the outside of the blender (and probably isn’t as sticky and gross as I might think), it's best to wipe this area down because you don't really have the option to fully submerge/soak it. Additionally, the way everything is connected— as others have pointed out, you cannot remove the blade section from the cup— makes thorough washing and drying more of a challenge than I’d prefer. It's kinda a game of "Is this one drink going to be worth the careful hand washing required?". And my lazy self pretty much answers: Nope.

I knew going in this wouldn’t rival a full size commercial blender in terms of its performance for ice. Yet the listing does state: “Powerful ice cube blending”. That’s their words, not mine. But the blades are teeny tiny and my ice cubes are admittedly beefy sized. For my other (corded) personal size blender I have to pre-crush my ice. I’m just a woman with her hammer, smashing some ice to kid glove her anemic blender. I like frozen drinks, not just milk or yogurt smoothies. So this is not really an upgrade from what I’ve been using. For mobility and to take into the office: 5 stars. For a simple yogurt and fruit smoothie or to whip up a protein powder, it may do you just fine. For ice and multi ingredients: I cannot enthusiastically recommend. It *does* have more power than you might think but they need to stop marketing this sort of teensy appliance for frozen drinks.

With a full size blender it requires a bit of finagling and you have to turn off the blender and use a spoon to push the bread back down into the blades a couple of times. With this little blender took a slice of bread a time and broke it into 4 parts and place it into the blender. Turned on the blender and then gave a gentle shake any time the bread got stuck. text: I received this Hamilton Beach Mini Cordless Portable Personal Blender in good condition in its cardboard product box. It is not heavy and doesn't take up alot of space. I ordered the "Pink" color variation and it looks just like it is pictured on here- a very light pink base and travel lid with handle. It comes with everything that is pictured, such as the USB-A to USB-C charging cable, plastic bladeguard/protein powder carrier, and the 16oz. shatterproof plastic BPA-free jar. It comes with an instruction booklet in different languages in both written and illustrated directions. Using this blender is easy and beginner friendly. It comes with some charge, but a full charge is recommended before your first use. It doesn't take a long time to fully charge. It has an indicator light that turns blue or red that flashes or stays still to indicate different meanings, such as charging and whether the jar is fully locked into the base and safe to start blending. You simply start by filling up your jar, with the instructions suggesting you go with liquid at the bottom up to the minimum liquid line, then ice, fresh produce, frozen produce, and finally any powder at the top. These altogether should not pass the maximum ingredients line. Then you twist the base onto the top of the jar lid, double press the start button, and flip it over. Each cycle turns off automatically at 30 seconds. You may need more than one cycle to fully blend your smoothie. I used my Orgain protein, which is particularly thick because it's made of pea protein, but this mini blender did a great job of fully blending my smoothie in two cycles. Keep in mind that this jar size won't accommodate larger smoothies or shakes, such as the capacity of a shaker bottle or Nutribullet. For me, this is enough and I think the price makes it a great way to start your health or fitness journey without investing alot of money. I have a Vitamix immersion blender to make smoothies in glass Mason jars, and they recommend cleaning the blender by placing it into the same Mason jar with warm soapy water so I will be cleaning this mini blender jar and base the same way.

title: Leaves Much to be Desired
text:
I don't expect much from a small portable blender other than it have the capability to blend a variety of things a normal person might choose to mix in such a device. This portable blender from Lacomri falls short of its ability to be such a blender.

Let's start with something basic, something I make on a routine basis: a powdered protein shake with peanut butter powder and ice. It's a drink I make a few times a week using a regular blender. And I realize that a mini-blender isn't going to match the power of a regular full-sized blender, but we’re talking small ice cubes + powdered drink + almond milk. And the instructions say “big ice cubes are acceptable”.

First off, the blender needs to be charged. It comes with a USB cord and takes an hour or so to get fully charged. Once charged it flashes “FU”, either insulting you or letting you know it’s charged. The unit is smaller and heavier than I expected. It can only be filled 4/5 full, so there’s not much room depending on what you put in a smoothie. With small ice chips filling about 1/4 of the cup, I could about 6-7 oz. of liquid in it. So when it says it holds 14 oz., that's not necessarily the amount you can blend. The top unscrews easily, and there is a filter-like piece inside it (assuming to strain seeds from fruit but the instructions are vague and are mostly warnings on what not to do). So, I added the shake and peanut butter powder and twisted the lid tight. It blinked “88” indicating that it was ready to blend. The instructions say to shake the device while blending, so that is what I did. It blended for 20 seconds and turned off. My assumption was that it was done, so I took the lid off to drink. It did a shotty job with grinding up the ice; there were large chunks stuck together. The cubes I used were no bigger than your average blueberry. I also found that clumps of my peanut butter powder had sunk to the bottom of the blender. Apparently, the blades couldn’t reach that, even with shaking. So I tried it two more times. By the end of the third try, the ice chunks were gone but still wound up with a couple clumps of powder mix.

The cleaning was easy for the lid. They instruct you to keep the base away from water and to put water in the cup and blend to clean it. I found it hard to keep the base entirely away from liquids since I was making a liquid drink and needed to put the glass under water to fill and empty the water.

Charging is easy. You can plug it into any USB port. As for sound, it is a little louder than I expected, but not quite as loud as a regular blender... more a “whining buzz” like you’d get from a propeller.

I do like that this comes with a separate cap. This enables you to mix your drink at home and take your prepared drink with you. Essentially, you to attach the cap to the opposite end of the cup, removing the bottom blender piece. However, there is nowhere to store the lid with the cup itself so I could easily see myself losing it. Ideally, there’d be a “hook” on it to attach it to the cup. Another flaw is the material the carrying strap is made of. If it gets wet while rinsing the top, it stays wet for hours; it’s not a quick dry material.

Overall, I give this blender 2.5 stars.

title: A remarkable blender with a lot of power and a well thought out design
text:
[[VIDEOID:bf70328253e34458aea8d8b91c27f674]] It’s like that “little engine that could” nursery story about that little train - this blender packs a huge power punch in such a small size that I did not believe it could do what it can at a mere 6watts of power.

It can blend ice as well. I did not expect this kind of quality but it is a name brand product: Hamilton Beach who also makes big blenders. I was totally surprised that this little thing can actually make everything you want in a larger blender just shrunken down in an individual serving size.

What’s cool about this is the fact you can run to your grocery store, pick up some fruits, a small bottle of milk, put it all inside this 16oz bottle, put on the motor, and blend it in about 30 seconds (max time) you’ll have a fully blended juice concoction. I mean it doesn’t get more fancy than this!

What I really like is the fact the motor can really blend hard to blend stuff - it can cut up the ice into bits so it will work on your frozen fruits too - even big blenders have some trouble with large frozen fruits so it’s easier on the motor if you let it defrost a bit rather use than straight out the freezer. The battery seems to last a long while - it says 28 blends per full charge - each blend is around 30 seconds max you can shorten this depending on the type of beverage you want. That’s a lot of blending for this small of a blender!

The cleanup is easier than ever - I just put a few drops of dish soap and put in some warm/hot water. Put the motor on and blend it for 30 seconds default. You’ll never have the problem of smelly blenders ever again using this method. You can’t dishwasher this thing and I don’t use the dishwasher anyway but you can rinse the motor after cleaning it this way with just water and it will always come out clean and neutral smelling.

This doesn’t come with a cookbook but you can simply blend any fruits and/or vegetables with juice or milk - I make iced coffee drinks and with the ice being crushed finely using this blender, this one is a keeper. Excellent well made individual sized blender that you can use literally anywhere.

The 16oz bottle with a cap is really well thought out - the cap can be used to hold the white measuring cup/motor cover for transport and then after use, the white measuring cup is used to cover the motor blades. Just very well thought out design all in one.

Lastly about the noise level it’s not ear deafening. It sounds like any blender you have except it’s not as loud. You can hear it (see the video) but it’s not offensively loud either. Another small concern is that I'd like to see Hamilton Beach address is to have replaceable accessories for this blender. Such as another 16oz cup for extra use.

Very EASY process:
+ Rinse Blender
+ Assemble BLEND BASE with CONTAINER
+ Add about 3/4 cup ice cubes
+ Add a shot of RUM to taste; slightly more than a shot of STRAWBERRY mix, to taste
+ Make sure TOP is secure
+ Make sure BOTTOM BLEND BASE is tight, with ARROW in center (green light will flash)
+ When GREEN LIGHT flashes, hold BASE and TOP and press START button
+ Pickup the whole blender while it's mixing and SHAKE it lightly to mix with ICE
+ Let it BLEND for about 20-30 secs
+ ALL DONE!

The coconut milk must have caused an electrical short. As I was dissembling the blender, it turned back on and cut my finger.

To make sure I hadn’t accidentally pressed “on”, I again turned it off and set it on the counter. After about 45 seconds it turned on again, with just the blades spinning and no cover. I tried turning it off again, it turned itself back on. It ended up going until the battery died.

I’m attaching photos of the milk leaking from the charging port, milk leaking from the top, and my cut finger.

Messy, useless, and actually very dangerous.

title: Compact Blender Cup For Small Batch Smoothies
text:
I like to make smoothies in the morning but hate dragging out the full sized blender. This blender cup makes a single serving quickly and easily. The bender runs in intervals so you don’t have to stop it yourself. If you need more time just push the button again for another round. You do have to do a little shaking but that doesn’t bother me. I used frozen fruit, a little yogurt, juice and super green powder and with some trial and error I got it all blended into a marvelous smoothie. I don’t use ice in my smoothies and didn’t feel that it struggled with the frozen fruit at all. Cleaning is very easy just rinse it off. The charge lasts a long time. I’ve been using it often and haven’t had to recharge yet. Very happy with this and for the price it’s a deal because unlike some others in the price range this one comes with a double walled insulated cup that keeps your drink frozen while you enjoy it. The only thing I don’t care for is the handle because it hangs down and is kind of in the way when trying to close the cup. Also I wish the lid had a hole in it for a straw. But neither of these would keep me from recommending this product.

Pro tip: Blending frozen fruit should be cut up into smaller bits and you should take care not to go over the fill line. It helps if you blend the first half and then add the second half and a little more liquid especially if using any kind of protein powder or greens powder.

title: Small portable blender
text:
Let's get this out of the way. This is not a powerful blender, but it's not fair to expect that out of anything so small. This is a portable rechargeable blender that can be used on the go. title: A Good Blender For Basic Smoothies/Shakes
text:
[[VIDEOID:484161c98cdd8141c4a6286a282b8a48]] Pleasantly surprised by this Mini Cordless Portable Personal Blender. I got this to use at work on occasion and so far, it's been fine, other than fussing with a clean-up. Luckily, we have a kitchen there which allows me to take the time to clean the blender properly after use.

So just to be sure it would work as advertised, I made my first smoothie from their list of recipes in the booklet, a Chocolate Raspberry Protein Shake. I added everything in order (which included frozen fruit), as per the instructions, hit the start button twice, flipped it over, and waited. After the first attempt, not everything was completely blended, see photos. I shook it up and started it again. I had to run it 3 times to be sure it was totally blended, as it only runs 30 seconds at a time and shuts off automatically. But the smoothie was yummy in the end.

Now comes the cleanup. So, when you take the base off after your smoothie is blended, you have smoothie all inside the base around the blade. Since the base also holds the battery, it's a bit tricky to clean. They suggest holding the blender base on its side, then carefully rinsing just the blades under running water. I was paranoid about getting water in the plug area, I'm not going to lie. I don't think I did, but it took a minute to be sure it was completely cleaned. There is a rubber nub where smoothie got stuck and I just hope that I cleaned it well enough. That isn't the best way to clean it, bad suggestion on their part. Instead, just rinse the jar, then add a little soap and water and blend that up. Then wipe the blade area off with a paper towel.

I tried another recipe (see video), a modified version of their Protein Packed Chocolate Peanut Butter Smoothie. I used frozen banana slices, and walnuts instead of peanut butter and added caramel syrup. Again, I had to blend it numerous times, stop and shake it, to be sure it was completely blended. It did a good job, and the smoothie was delicious!

For a mini blender, if you don't get all crazy and stuff lots of ingredients in it, I think it's okay. I don’t feel it is a super powerful blender. The charging cord is 2’ long, which is a good size. I should also mention, something in the base rattles on my blender. I'm not sure if it's supposed it, but it still works. My only drawback for this is cleaning it, but otherwise, it does the job.

title: Solid, robust portable blender for smoothies!
text:
As a chef (for my wife and 3 young adult daughters) I originally got this to blend fresh seasoning for cooking. When this portable blender arrived, I happily opened it, set it up and was ready to put it to good use - blending my seasonings. After all, fresh seasoning is important for exquisite taste! Well, before I was able to blend my first mix, my lovely daughter, home from college walked into the kitchen and promptly claimed the pinkish blender for smoothies. No arguments, no questions!

It was my fault really, maybe I should not have gotten pink. Led by my wife, they set about making a smoothie. They added frozen blueberries, strawberries, bananas, acai, grape, apple and a few other “healthy “ stuff. This blender came with a flat ice tray that made tiny half-round ice buttons. My wife added a bit of honey and vanilla, then threw in all the ice from the tray, screwed the lid down, and mixed it all up by shaking.

To start the blender, it required that the unit be tilted about 45 degrees or more before pressing the power button (I figured that part out). The unit motor sounded strong, and mixed that smoothie quite well. It has 6 blender blades, 2 of which are serrated. That is unusual and highly commendable!
The cup is labeled “BPA free” and has a tight fitting screw cover. The bottom of the cup sits on a wide and solid washer seal that has not leaked since using it.

The result was a thick 2-cups of really good smoothie that was a generous serving for an adult. I snuck a taste and it was surprisingly pretty good. Everything was blended well. The machine automatically stopped after about 40 seconds. It could be stopped before if you want chunkier pieces though, or can be run again for a smoother mix. I noticed that the ice gets crushed best when the unit is placed upright on a flat surface so the ice gets down towards the blender blades. It’s good to shake the blender ever so often while blending. Prevents chunks.

This thing is travelling with us on our beach vacations. I figure we will make some single serve, frozen, pre-made ziplock bags of smoothie fruit to take with us. We’ll just add juice.

After use, cleanup was very easy. No mess - no fuss. The blender charges with a USB-A to USB-C cable that is included. We will need to also carry an extra USB 5-volt, 2.4-amps (at least) charger transformer brick. It seems that most everything these days does not include a power supply charger brick. No problem though. This good looking, robust and functional portable blender is very worth having.

title: Can't get it to work.
text:
When I first received this blender, I read the instructions that stated it needed to be fully charged before first use. I charged it overnight and then didn't need to use it until the following week, so I didn't get to try it immediately.
However, when I went to first use it, I loaded up my ingredients, followed all of the instructions, and hit the button to start it....but nothing happened. I tried multiple times to get it to start, then looked up in the instructions what the red blinking lights meant. The instructions stated that the blinking lights I was seeing indicated that it needed to be charged. I was a little disappointed since I had FULLY charged it, never used it, and the battery was dead already, but I just figured it must not last long on standby. That could get annoying, but if you develop a habit of plugging it in each day, it's not a dealbreaker.

However, what IS a deal breaker is when you fully charge it again, then load up all your ingredients that night, push the start button, and have the same thing happen. Same red blinking lights (and to be clear, depending on how many times the red light blinks, it can mean different things, but this was the same exact error as before, indicating that it needed to be charged). So if I can leave it on the charger for 5+ hours, try to use it no less than 2 hours after removing it from the charger, and I still get that error, there is obviously a problem.

I really cannot rate how effectively it blends since I literally haven't been able to use it. The only thing I've been able to do is fill with ingredients that I then end up having to transfer to my full-size blender since this won't work...and that obviously defeats the purpose since my entire goal was to use a smaller blender for the things that don't require a full-size blender.

It's also worth noting that because the battery, motor and blades are all in the top, it is quite top heavy when sitting empty. Not a big deal, but if you bump it, you an expect it to fall over pretty easily.

Based on my experience, I would say to skip this product altogether. Mine is headed to the trash, as it's useless to me if it won't turn on.

title: Pretty great with a few caveats
text:
Every morning, I make a milkshake with milk, Muscle Milk powder, one banana and 3-4 ice cubes. Getting out a big blender can be a real pain, so I was excited to get this one. It's perfect for making milkshakes.

Here are some key points:
- It has a built-in rechargeable battery and it's nice that you don't have to plug it into the wall. One charge easily lasts for 3-4 blending sessions
- It blends pretty well but not amazingly. What I tend to do is lift it up and tilt the whole thing while blending. That helps with the banana (which I also tear up into 5 chunks)
- It's much much quieter than my previous Ninja blender, which is great.

There is one downside, and you can see it in my picture. The main "cup" isn't actually a cup. It has a hole for the base and the lid. So if you want to take your cup to go, you have to do this:
1. Attack the cub to the blending base
2. Add your ingredients
3. Put the lid on
4. Blend
5. Turn the whole thing upside down, and remove the base
6. Attach the bottom cap

The whole turning thing upside is a little strange, and it can potentially make a little mess. Alternatively, you could just pour it into another container.

I would NOT add sticky stuff (like peanut butter) into the blender. You can't put the blender in the dishwasher (and it's sharp), so you'll want to keep things simple so that you can rinse off the blender with hot water.

Anyway, this is great for making milkshakes once you get the hang of things.

Thanks for reading! I hope you found this review helpful!
