We kindly note that the personal blender you bought from us has been shipped by Amazon. For better use of this product, please note that:
1. For first-time use, please charge the personal blender for 3 hours, and the indicator light will turn blue.
2. Please put fruit and liquid less than the max line.
3. Do not put hot food or liquid over 122℉ in the juice cup to stir.
4. The product is set to work 40s each time, you can press the button to stop it as you wish.
5. Please dry the personal blender first before covering the lid
6. If you are trying to mix powder, mix it into the liquid first, then pour it into the machine before blending with the other ingredients.

Really sorry about the inconvenience.

title: If you are looking at this, you know what you want...
text:
My family loves juicing. Some people may not actually consider this a juicer because in their minds juicers extract and separate the juice from the pulp. This machine is more of a juicing blender in that it makes a blend of juice and pulp. That said, it still makes a nutritious drink of whatever you put in it. It can also be used to mix fluid and powdered mixes (powdered soy milk or mixing carob powder with almond milk, etc).

I still haven't quite figured out the straw. I believe the flanged part goes under the lid but it doesn't seem to hold well there although it allows for closing. Oh well, whether I use the straw or not is optional. The components are quite well made and the wrist strap is high quality showing the commitment of the company.

The dots on the powered lid must match the dot on the bottle for the blades to operate. But check and make sure that your purchase does not allow the blades to turn when off the bottle or serious injury could occur (again, this would only happen with a manufacturing error).

The button operates with two quick presses (read the manual or you might think you bought a dud).

BPA free and takes liquids below 100C (below boiling). Comes with USB cable but you might need to buy a USB to AC adapter (most phones use one).

Very nice. Highly recommend!

title: Great blender does the job
text:
As I am new to blending and smoothies, this rechargeable blender seemed to be a good size to try out. The way the blender cup body is made gives it a nice look, has the appearance of being sturdy and feels well made.
I found a simple recipe with spinach, frozen banana slices, peanut butter and almond milk that I wanted to make. I was not sure if the peanut butter would blend well or just get stuck to the inside of the blender. I added all the ingredients and pushed the button and I was surprised to see that it all blended very well, even the peanut butter. The instructions said to tilt it back and forth but I didn't really need to move it around much. The six blades handled the job with ease.
It's easy to charge and you can see at a glance how much charge it has by the number of red lights around the top of the blender base. A full charge will show all green lights. Unless it is aligned properly, the motor will not start which is a great safety feature. Once done mixing, I turn it over, unscrew the blender base and screw on the included cup base. The pop up drinking spout cover means I can mix and drink on the go.

title: I like it
text:
I have never made smoothies before and when I came across this portable USB blender I thought it would be a good opportunity to give it a try. The first thing I noticed when I took it out of the box is that it seemed pretty small.
The blender charged pretty quickly with the included USB cord. With a recipe provided in the user manual I gathered the various ingredients for a smoothie, added them to the blender and pressed the button. The first time I tried it, it did not start. I then figured out that I had tightened it a little too much and went past the arrow (that I could not see). So I backed it up a little to line up the arrows and it started right up. Then I marked both arrows with a black permanent marker so they would be more visible. The logo is made to stand out so it would seem to me that they could do the same with the arrows. It seemed slow to start, although I'm not sure if it may have been because I was using frozen fruit. It is suggested frozen fruit should be thawed first. Once it got going, it mixed the ingredients well. I did have to move it back and forth to keep the ingredients moving around as the user manual stated. It made a delicious smoothie.
I wish the size of the cup was a little bigger. I found myself wanting to make another smoothie as the first one was just not quite enough.
It was easy to clean. I rinsed the cup and bottom cap, added warm water and a couple drops of Dawn, screwed on the blending base and turned it on. This did a good job of cleaning the base. Then I just hand washed the rest, although the user manual says you can put them in the dishwasher.

The mini ice cube tray is gimmicky. It’s a pain to use and a lot of trouble for a tiny amount of ice. It also defeats the purpose of a portable system. The cheap cleaning brush is junk. Just unscrew the container from both ends and use a normal sponge.

Protip for use - unscrew the bottom power unit, not the top, to drink.

title: Beautiful looking blender, but not an ideal design
text:
I haven't used a lot of electronic kitchen appliances, but generally speaking, most of them look the same and don't have any especially beautiful or fun designs. You can already imagine it in your head if I were to say to you, "Picture a blender or food processor." Did you think of a black and/or gray item with a conventional design?

That's where this personal blender is a real winner. The color is beautiful and eye-catching, the built-in lights indicate when the cup is aligned with the base, and the cup has a multi-faceted design that adds visual interest. I could look at this blender all day, and the strap, though it could be longer to accommodate someone perhaps putting their whole hand in, is cute too.

However, once you get past the looks, you find that there are some issues with this blender that make it potentially unsafe, or less than convenient. The first is the fact that the blade is permanently attached to the motor/base. This blender holds a charge as well, when it's not connected to a power source. This means that 1. the blender is harder to clean because you can't remove the blades and 2. If the base were to malfunction, you could potentially cause a dangerous situation where someone gets cut by the whirring blade because they think there's no longer any power in the base, or if the base simply malfunctions and spins even when the cup's not on. It would have been 1000% safer to make this blade detachable, or part of a lid that gets screwed into the base with the cup on top, like some other personal blender designs. Another gripe is with the fact that you have to add liquids to a certain level and cut pieces of fruit to a certain size, as well as avoid adding certain types of fruits to the machine. All these restrictions can be less than convenient, and limit the potential of what you could use for this blender. If you're advertising an item as something you can use on the go, but you ask people to follow all these restrictions, I think that would make it hard to be something that is truly portable and easy to use. A lot of frozen fruit pieces don't come in the small size suggested, so you'd have to diligently cut that fruit down to size before bringing it with you or using it in the blender, and so on.

I also found the instructions a little sparse, more safety warnings and details would have been helpful.

Once I did use it to make a few smoothies, I found that it was effective in creating a drinkable smoothie, if you blended long enough and respected the restrictions outlined in the instructions. I'm just not eager to use it all the time because of everything discussed in this review. I see this as a great backup blender to my regular, powerful personal blender I already have. I am also thinking to use it as a food processor to make pesto, which I think might be possible based on what the listing suggests, but it would have been nice for the instructions to fully address the possibility of food processing and perhaps even offer a recipe idea or two.

Beautiful item, really cute, but could have used some improvements in the design and instructions. Would be worth checking out if you want something nice looking for the office, and you'd definitely receive a compliment if someone saw you using this in the kitchen, but it's not the ideal item if you were only going to limit yourself to one personal blender for your household.

title: Pulverizes my fruit just fine (until it doesn't)

[[VIDEOID:732e8a460dd0642eedd429df362620c9]] Update: Despite my first positive review, this Doshabal blender keeps malfunctioning. It won't consistently work and I couldn't figure out why. And believe me I tried everything. So, I was so tired of it making me irritated, I am giving it away. You often will have what you pay for, and next time I order a personal blender, I'm shelling out more money for it to have a better more consistent one.

------

This Doshabel personal blender works very well and offers a more sturdy and effective blender than the cheaper one I previously ordered (you often do have what you pay for).

I did overfill this on first use, just to see what it was capable of (I included a video). I stuffed it with fresh fruit and yogurt with just a little water and though I had to shake it a couple of times, it pulverized my smoothie ingredients within 30 to less than 60 seconds.

I don't usually add ice to mine but I experimented by adding quite some small ice cubes and a little water and let it go for the 30 seconds. Though it didn't pulverize all the ice, it did mush up quite a bit. Another 30 seconds or two and it would have it all done.

To make it work you have to line up the arrow to where the lights are so do note that, or it won't work.

Has 4 upper blades, two of which are serrated. Has two lower blades. So six blades in all.

The pink color is pretty--not a baby pink exactly but soft pink.

The container comes off the unit so it can be washed (as does the top). You have to wash the motor part by hand. The container fills about a 10-12 oz or so glass.

One thing I wish is that they had a cover to put over the charging port. You have to rinse the motor part (can't put that in the dishwasher so don't), and I have to put my finger over the port to keep water out.

It comes with a metal straw and cleaning sponge.

It came charged but I still charged it. I am curious how long it'll keep a charge, and I'll come back to report if it doesn't keep a charge as they indicate.

title: Kinda small and a little hard to clean, but it works well.
text:
The tank holds 18.5 ounces. That means about a 16oz shake if you fill it clear full. It only has one speed. I made a milkshake (vanilla, so there was no fruit to chop up and mix in). I put the milk in first, then spoonfuls of fairly soft, hard ice cream. It was not difficult at all to scoop out of the carton. When I turned it on all it did was to stir up the milk. So I inverted it a couple of times and then shook it a little to settle the ice cream. When the ice cream settled the blades stopped cold. I shut it off, then inverted it and restarted it, like it said to do in the instructions. That worked so I inverted it several times to keep settling the unstirred ice cream. After adding some more milk it finally made a somewhat runnier milkshake than I normally like. I didn’t time it but seemed to take well less than a minute.

With as much strain as the ice cream gave it, I decided not to try crushing ice cubes. Did it perform as advertised? Yes. Was it easy too get all of the shake out? Not really. Was it as easy to clean s they said? No. I ran it a couple of times with water and ended up using a bottle brush with detergent to get all of the residue out of the jar. The base does not disassemble so I had to clean the blades in the base.

Can you do other things while it is working? No. Does it take a lot of attention while it is running? Constantly. Will it replace my countertop blender? Not on your life. First when I finally do have a shake I like to make one out of a whole can of root beer and about quarter carton of ice cream. After I set it and forget it while it mixes, I am probably melting real butter for the air-pop popcorn and setting up a movie. Afterwards the glass jar seems to get most of the shake out easier. Rinse it once and throw it in the dishwasher, including the blade assembly. That’s easy to clean.

But you can use this one on the fly, in the car, as you are working out, etc. You can take it with you, doing whatever. The smaller size would be convenient for baby food also. But my babies have babies of their own that all seem to be past that stage.

So for my usage, I’m just not about to ask my wife to find a spot in her crowded kitchen for it. For you it may be just what you need. Oh, and by the way, the shake did taste great.

title: Love it
text:
A DeFyned Blender is a convenient and portable option for those who want to blend their drinks or smoothies on the go. It's compact and lightweight, which makes them easy to carry around in a backpack or travel bag. They are also perfect for camping trips or outdoor activities where there is no electricity available.
However, some drawbacks to consider are that battery-operated blender may not be as powerful as regular electric blenders, and the battery life may be limited. Additionally, they may not be suitable for blending hard or frozen ingredients.
Overall, if you're looking for a portable and convenient option for blending your drinks, no need to look elsewhere, just make sure to read product specifications before purchasing to ensure it meets your needs.

title: Super cool gadget!!!
text:
Couldn’t wait for it to arrive - carrying my countertop Vitamix+100ft extension cord is not fun:)
On a serious note, first let me start with things I don’t like - get it out of the way:)
The entire unit does not fit in my car/truck cup holders - 3 1/2in bottom; detached cup does. The whole unit however fits nicely in the compartment box beside the cup holders.
The blender only runs when unplugged from USB.
…
Now, the good stuff:)
Load it up with frozen fruits+milk or such and play with it like a bartender would with cocktails. It will pulverize everything if not in the first 30sec increment then second or third.
My googling says it’s got the most powerful motor out there - 240w; the most RPM’s - 26k!
I make smoothies every day in my Vitamix, Ninja or Nutribullet; the thing that kills me is watching them go to waste in my fridge/ice box/ice bag or cup holder - thick foam forms on top, the rest is sugary water after an hour or 2. Try feeding that to your finicky 7yr old!:)
This blender solves the problem - make it on the spot after soccer practice, gym or on the beach! Preload it, put it in a cooler (minus the motor of course); 1 or 2 hrs later you’re good to go! Frozen stuff won’t spoil even in a car cup holder, at least not for a while.
As a countertop guy my biggest worry is how to get creative with this blender - hiking, work, outdoor patio or just as a backup to my countertops:) Fun all around!

title: A rechargeable battery powered blender
text:
It works.

Battery power is generally a compromise on appliances with rare expensive exceptions (thnk Dyson vacs) and the need for portability in the device must significantly outweigh the shortcomings for it to be a worthwhile thing.

The shortcomings here are substantial. It's not going to be able to service your party from a remote electricity-free bar. At best, you will be able to make a few drinks, a malted or some other things before you need to feed it more electrons. The battery is not nearly as long lasting in regular use (blending iced drinks for example) as the seller says. Or at least, that is my experience.

If being able to blend stuff far from an electric outlet is important to you, I cannot think of another way to do it.

title: Such a perfect little portable blender!
text:
We love this blender so much that it's almost replaced our great home blender that we have, because of how convenient it is to use. I was impressed just taking it out of the box. It's adorable and pretty heavy duty feeling. The colors are great, and I love that you can drink out of the blending container with the included accessories. It cuts down on how many dishes I have to wash and is so easy to clean. My daughter makes at least one smoothie a day, so I was having to wash the big blender and her glass, usually multiple times a day. Now when she gets done, she can quickly wash this one herself and I don't have to do anything. Its small size makes it easier and less cumbersome to use than the big blender as well.

It blends our frozen fruit and nugget ice great. The little silicone ice tray that they included was a nice bonus surprise if you don't have smaller ice at home. I haven't tried larger pieces of ice. I'm impressed with its battery life and how powerful it is to be so small. I love it's look and portability!

You do have to make sure that it's lined up properly in order for it to work, but that's a great safety feature in my opinion. It helps us to put our liquids in first, then fruit, then ice. We like to give it a little shake while it's going and it keeps us from having to open it up and get anything frozen unjammed. I suggest making sure the lid is screwed on tight because we've given a shake and made a mess before. It will still work with the lid off.

This little blender is great. We've gotten a lot of use out of it already and 10/10 recommend it! It's as efficient as it is adorable.

text: [[VIDEOID:e3baeaf70e540ad230c3abbfce85e0a9]] Let me start by saying that I REALLY like this little blender.  It is the perfect machine for making single-serving sized ice cream milkshakes.  Having bought this product for precisely that reason, I consider this machine to be a 5-star item.  However, this product comes with an unexpected accessory.  There is a blue, silicone miniature ice cube tray included with the blender.  This device makes ice cubes that are one half inch on all sides which is REALLY tiny.  I’m guessing that the ice cubes need to be that small in order for this blender to make a smoothie or a crushed ice juice drink.  The reason that this really bothers me is that no mention is made of this anywhere in the listing or the directions for this product.  You are led to believe that this machine will crush regular sized ice cubes when it cannot.  It did a GREAT job of breaking down and blending ice cream and milk to make the perfect milkshake, but I’d be wary of its ability to make anything requiring ice.  Also, the little silicone ice cube form only makes enough ice for one smoothie so be prepared to make several batches of ice beforehand if you plan on making drinks for you and your friends.

title: A good little battery powered blender, but a couple minor flaws
text:
This is a nice little battery powered blender that is easy to take on the go/travel and does a pretty good job, but it does have some (potential) flaws. It has a decent capacity and never seemed to struggle with anything I blended, but I did keep it relatively simple and didn’t try to grind up anything too hard (e.g., ice, nuts, coffee grounds, etc.). Compared to shaker bottles, this little blender is fantastic and makes short work of mixing up my shakes or smoothies and it does a better job. Compared to a full size blender, it is lacking in some features, but the inclusion of a pulse mode is nice and will get things done for the most part.

The blender I received is slightly different than what is pictured in that the clear container is transparent blue and has a bit of a pattern to it (not just smooth). It comes with a USB B to USB C cable for charging (no power supply though, so you need to use one you already have to buy one separately), a bottom that can be put on in place of the blender motor/blade, and a manual. Also not depicted in the photos is an additional strap that is attached to the back of the lid. I removed this as there is a plastic, fold down carry loop built into the lid as well, so I didn’t see the need for the redundancy or having it flop around and get in the way.

The blender has two modes: blend, and pulse. There are LEDs around the top of the blender portion (base of the clear portion) that light up and indicate that the unit is running, what the charge is, and what mode it is in. It also will flash red when the clear container is not seated all the way down (there is a magnet that needs to align with the power button). When in blend mode, it is a steady green ring of lights, pulse mode has a yellowish-green set of alternating lights, and when you stop the unit it will show a combination of green (charge) and red (discharge) LEDs to indicate battery charge.

The base of the blender (motor, battery, and blade) can be removed and replaced with a simple base that can be used after you blend everything up and want to transform this blender into a standard bottle. Both the blender base and the regular bottom have rubber rings on the bottom to keep it firmly planted on any surface and not slide around (although, I do generally find with tall containers like this that not sliding around sometimes just means it tips over instead). The one issue I have with the base is that the rubber ring that seals it does not seal at the top of the threads, but rather at the bottom, so liquid will get into the threads, which means when you go to swap bases or if you don’t clean it right away, you will have a little bit of a mess there that may get sticky and could make it hard to unscrew later.

The lid fits on nice and secure and has a pop top that you can pour or drink from. There is a little hole that also allows air to get in and keep from building a vacuum and causing glugging (so it pours smoothly). The flip top part of the lid has silicone rubber seals that I found work well to keep it all sealed tight and everything contained inside. However, the little rubber seal the covers the small vent hole does not stay on very well and I’ve almost lost it a few times (and once just about down the garbage disposal), so I tend to just take it off when cleaning and clean it separately so as not to loose it. The flip top has a bar/ring that flips up over the end near the release button that keeps it from accidentally being released when using the blender (like locking it in place). The entire lid can be unscrewed to gain easy access to the cup portion of the blender to make it easy to add ingredients.

I like this little blender and find it very convenient. I like that this is battery powered and USB recharged because it really doesn’t matter what country you go to, USB power is standard. It blends well and is easy to clean. Sure tipping it upside down and swapping bottoms seems a little odd at first, but it does make it convenient to use the same container as a normal bottle instead of having to dirty up another cup/mug/bottle just to transfer the blended beverage into something to drink out of (and I’ve found myself being lazy and just drinking out of it with the blender attachment still on it). Even though the placement of the bottom seal could be better (I think two seals would be even better), it never leaked on me and I tended to clean it right away, so I never had to deal with it getting crusty or sticky. And, so long as you remember to remove the one little rubber stopper/seal from the flip top when cleaning, you should be good not loosing it when washing everything (for washing, I just put in a little dish soap, some water, and hit blend). The only other thing I wish it had was more markings for different fill levels (mL and oz) instead of just “MAX” and “600ML.” It also lasts for several drinks on one charge (I’ve made a few shakes and only used one bar of charge, but heavier loads like fresh fruit may use more charge), so I think this would be good for travel, camping, picnics, etc. and not just a mini blender for kitchen use. I would recommend this and plan on using it quite regularly, so we will see how well it holds up to the continued daily abuse I plan to put it through.

title: impressive power room for some improvements
text:
It is an interesting and potentially very useful concept. First, the blending is actually impressive and powerful. The charging is USB. It will not function while it is connected to the charger. At the price (just under $46 at time of this review) it is not inexpensive nor a bargain.
In order to start it you have to press the power button twice. So I could see people (especially people that forego instructions) getting frustrated with it or assuming it doesn't work. There is also a safety feature where the container body has to be properly tightened onto the base before it can be turned on.
After use I found myself wondering if I should leave the base on with the blended contents inside or if I should detach it and turn the container over - because only one end can be completely covered when detached from the base. This leads me to the next issue /question: the product pictures show people on the go, at the gym etc. They show a lady drinking from the container. But only one end can be capped. So why not include a second end cap with the kit so that you can blend your stuff and then not lug the base around or even so that you can recharge the base while you are on the go? Also at this price I would like to see a power block included with the USB cable.
Overall it is fairly innovative and impressive power with some room for improvement.

The top isn't completely sealed, I discovered that there's a tiny hole that allows liquid to come out during my attempt to move the ice around by inverting the blender. title: Good for travel, but you don't want this as your main smoothie blender.
text:
In a pinch, this will get the job done but there are too many compromises to make it your main smoothie blender. First, the blender can only hold 300ML (roughly 10 Oz) of ingredients. So, unless your drink is only liquid and powder (protein or pre-workout or whatever), you're not going to be able to put much into the cup. Any solid foods will quickly make the contents reach the 300ML fill line, and if you add more than that it will spill over when putting on the blender lid.

Also, as others have pointed out, the blades are small and pretty close to the lid which makes it hard to cut larger objects down. I definitely wouldn't trust it with regular size ice cubes or even frozen fruits. Last, cleaning it is more trouble than it should be due to the blades being on the lid which means hand washing, and trying to make sure you don't immerse the whole thing on accident.

Having said that, I will definitely keep this for travel purposes when I'm probably not toting around frozen fruits and stuff anyway.

title: Had it for a year. Used 2x week. Strainer lid is the dealbreaker.
text:
I wanted to like this blender but after having it for over a year now I feel it is time to replace it with something else.

The GOOD: The unit is built well and blends decently for what I need it for. I use it to blend protein powder into water with the occasional soft fruit. Charge it fully and it will serve you well for light blending and smoothies.

The BAD: The charging cover refuses to stay on and I lost it in the first week. A small piece of painters tape now covers my charge port.

The UGLY: I absolutely despise the lid. It is the worst part of the product and a pain to wash. It contains a large screw on lid that contains a strainer. The strainer screws onto the plastic blender and the lid screws onto that. Every time you blend something you have to take it apart and clean both lid and strainer separately and completely or you will collect chunks of unblended food inside the lid. This is a huge flaw and the reason I am replacing it. It would have been nice to be able to remove the strainer and have the lid screw directly onto the blender thus removing the compartment and making it 100 times easier to clean. For this main reason I am rejecting this product after a year of use.

It would be a 4 star product if the lid did not have the strainer or if the strainer was removable.

title: Best portable blender device I've used so far.
text:
I've owned two of these blender bottle devices and so far this one is the pre-eminent design of those type products. The containment barrel is completely removable and made of glass, so you can actually clean the barrel, with whatever you want (sponge scour-pad), without worrying about damaging gaskets or blades. Additionally this prevents your fingers from being near blades that could potentially just activate on you.

Onto the the motor and blade assembly, which has a nice feature of being unable to turn on unless the barrel is screwed onto the motor-blade assembly. This is done via a peep-hole and light sensor in that assembly, should that become blocked you could turn on the blades while they are exposed to whatever, so make sure that peep-hole is unobstructed while cleaning the base.

The last cool as knees benefit, that this device has to offer once again stems from the detachable barrel because you cap off the barrel with the included two different caps. So instead of carrying around your smoothie and motor assembly, you can just carry around the smoothie. Hugh weight saver.

The only issue I have with this product is that the included carry handle is completely plastic, which feels brittle and i definitely think would be the first point of failure on this device. Other products use an elastic band that is folded over itself and riveted to the cap, which, in my opinion, is the superior carry handle. Still it's a very minor grievance compared to the complete product. Highly recommend.

title: Struggles a bit with big chunks, but overall very good.
text:
The blade on this is a little small, so it seems to struggle a bit if you've got anything too big. We threw some strawberries, bananas, milk and a bit of crushed ice in for a very simple smoothie. It handled almost everything flawlessly, but one of the strawberries with a real big one, and that one didn't get blended at all despite the blender being held upside down, rotated, shaken a bit, etc to make sure everything was moving nicely.

So chopping that one in half did the trick and it was blended fine. As long as you're not throwing anything abnormally large in here, it appears to do the job well! It's got a surprising amount of power for the size and for being battery-operated. It seals nicely and as you can see, you double tap the power button to start it to prevent mishaps. You also only have to press it once to turn it off.

It comes with a separate lid, so you've got your blending lid and your smoothie cup lid, both screw on quite securely. The blending lid is very easy to wash off and the blade's small size also makes it easy to clean.

You lift up that bright orange tab to charge it, and the first charge takes a few hours. Battery life seems pretty good. After a full charge we've made multiple smoothies and it's still going strong. It refuses to turn on unless it's properly screwed onto the cup, which is a very good safety feature. I tried multiple times to get it to turn on without being screwed on, but even halfway screwed on to the actual cup wasn't enough, it had to be on fairly tightly.

A very good little portable blender for making smoothies on the go. It's not going to replace a high-end home blender, but it's perfect for work or picnics or whenever you might find a use for it outside the home. Or in your bedroom if you're real lazy!

title: Great Portable Blender!
text:
This is a pretty neat little blender. Charge it up and take it on the go! I didn't realize you could purchase pods for it till I opened it up and read the literature. I did search for them on Amazon but couldn't find them so I guess you must purchase them directly from Vejo's website. So I did some powder blending and it worked perfect. I put it thought the test to see if it would make me an Orange Julius blending a iced drink. Well it did chop the ice but still left some chunks in it. I think if I would of used crushed ice it would of done a perfect job. I know it says powder drink, but it doesn't not say you can put ice in it....and I was curious.
The blade spins at a decent speed but not like your plug in blender sitting on your counter. But that's the best part of this....you get to take it on the road with you. And when you want a blended drink you can make it right then and there. Not at home and then hours later drink it for lunch at the office or gym. It does work great with fresh fruit..but there are times the blade will get stuck but nothing a quick shake of the unit won't fix. Depending on what I'm blending I can get 4 to 6 shakes out of it on a single charge. Charging takes about 2 hours so it's a pretty fast charge with a USB-C input (cord only included). The finish in the unit has a soft rubbery feel to it so it feels nice in your hands. Cleans up super easy by hand, let it dry charge it up, and you're ready to go. The capacity is 12 oz so its not huge by any means but it is a perfect size for a blended drink. All in all, its a great little portable blender.

Note: The instructions say to only use it with their pods but I have yet to use it that way – I just use loose powder.

I love making matcha lattes by mixing matcha powder and milk. I've tried many different ways to combine them, including using a milk frother, but no matter what you can still feel the powder, until now! I put in my matcha powder, add milk to the 7oz line, and push the button. It comes out so smooth (you can't feel the powder at all) and there's no powder left on the bottom of the bottle when I'm done drinking it. The blend time when you push the button is 30 seconds and it's much quieter than I expected it to be. I love that I can blend it right before driving to work and then it fits in my car cup holder and I can drink it on my drive (I could blend it in my car if I really wanted to!).

To clean it I just put a drop of dawn in the bottle, add water to between the two fill lines, and let it blend. Then I rinse it out, rinse out the cap, and I'm done! The instructions say to clean it with a foam brush, but I tried that once and it just got caught on the blades and ripped the foam.

I will say that I'm very disappointed with their customer service. They have no phone number to call and I sent them an email 9 days ago and haven't heard back.

There is nothing for me to grab onto and the base of the carafe section is stuck, so I can no longer attach it onto the blender section. Pros:
+able to blend frozen blueberries and frozen strawberries perfectly
+large size to make a pretty big smoothie, not just single serve
+flip top seals well for travel. Straw fits in opening or you can sip from the top.
+Easy to clean, if you can get the pieces apart (see below for details in CON section)

Cons:
-You really have to twist the container into the base for it to lock in place. There are marking that have to line up and if you don't twist it into place it wont work. Seemed to loosen up after a few tries.
- The top of the bottle is a little small to load ingredient in, especially yogurt and peanut butter. So, I had to flip it over and load it from the bottom. This created another problem because the blender was unstable and wouldn't stand on its own without falling over.
- The ultimate con is that I can no longer unscrew the bottom cover of the portable jar. Thus, I can no longer screw the jar onto the main base with the blade. There is almost nothing to grab onto. I will try it in my workbench vice and see if that works. The base is made of plastic, a little non-slip surface would be nice. For the record, I am a physically fit 40ish yo male, pretty decent grip strength. I cant open it even using rubber cap openers etc... So right now it is a worthless item sitting on my counter. title: Portable.  I'll be using it often.
text:
It's difficult to separate my views on my excellent at home unit (a different brand) and this as a portable unit.

I've never experienced a portable unit, so I have nothing to compare it to in that respect.

I give it 4 stars simply because I have no experience with other portable blenders. It may indeed be a 5 star, I'll know that in the future as I test out other products I come across.

This will work brilliantly with fresh (wet or softish) ingredients which is exactly what I need when I am out and about due to my (some would call it "difficult" food intake requirements) sensitivities to food products and my physiological need to intake food about every 3 to 4 hours.

The cutting blades didn't make it through my dried date (which is what I use for sweetening) even though I cut it up into smallish pieces. It might have had I run it through another time or two. However, my at home version also has issues with that and it's a powerhouse -- so my usual way around this is to pre-soak a date or three in advance. I can easily carry the presoak in my bento lunch container (or any other container that keeps it moist and doesn't burst).

I recommend washing (or at least rinsing out) immediately or it will become a horror fest to clean (I found this out on my home machine and don't intend to replicate it out in the "wild" of the city or the parks, or the campground.

Speaking of campground -- this charges easily with a c- cord, so it's easy for me to hook up to one of my (many) portable power banks and recharge.

Moving on to the capacity -- I was surprised. I used 1 cup of water in my example photo, a fresh banana, some frozen berries, along with powders/vitamin supplements/dry ground chocolate -- and wound up with 2 cups of food. Yes, it may look funny, however, I'm cacao binging today and thus it's very brown.

This is perfect for a serving for me.

I didn't weigh it, so I cannot corroborate that it weighs 1.37 lbs, however, I can say, it is lightweight. I can carry it hooked by its strap/lanyard to a daypack or large back; I can carry it inside of a pack/bag; or I could use the wrist strap to carry it -- that doesn't suit me, yet that's a personal choice, and I know folks who would like that capability. The wrist strap/lanyard is sturdy and well made.

To use the bottom lid (to drink on the spot without carrying a glass/cup mechanism) all I did was to upend the blender, unscrew and unhook the blender cup from the blender base and put on the bottom lid. Then I upended it again and was able to use it as a drinking container.

I like this! It won't do everything, however, in my estimation it's not meant to. It's to use in portable situations and circumstances, and it does that VERY well.

I rate it 5 stars for my personal use, however, since I have nothing to compare it to industry-wide, I give it 4 starts until I come across another unit to test it against.

This is now one of my go-to personal lunchbox tools. I recommend highly.

.

title: Don't Let The Small Size Full You
text:
This blender may be 1/4 the size of a 6 blender, but it packs full-size power!

Pros:
1. Good seals, so there was no leakage noted!
2. Strong motor did a very good job of mixing items both with and without ice!
3. Using the blender was super simple with one button operation
4. It has a timed shutoff, so you don't have to guess or wait, start it up, and take care of other tasks.
5. The device does have lights: one on power button (good to see button) the other where the cup and base attach (they spin let you know it is running and done) which is good if you are hearing impaired
6. Conversly, if you are visually impaired, there is still an easily audible blending sound, which is not terrible...for a blender!
7. It is surprisingly light even with the blender attached, or you can take off that attachment and screw on the standard bottom, and you're even lighter and more mobile!
8. Yes, it comes in multiple colors, but I went with Johnny Cash black!
9. Top it all off with wireless operation, fast charging, and a very reasonable price, and you have a winner of a blender!

Cons: None

title: Nice blender to have, but so difficult to use
text:
This portable blender has some power to it as far as blending goes but getting to that point (blending) is an obstacle! The blender has a silicone gasket in the bottom that one would naturally presume is there to prevent leakage, HOWEVER it is that very gasket that makes it near impossible to fully 'lock' the canister in place so that you don't get that infernal "ER" reading/beeping every single time (ugh)! There is no manner of canister placement onto the base that makes any difference at all in trying to line up the arrows for a full lock. No matter what, you have to excessively overturn the canister to get those arrows to line up - I couldn't do it, had to have my husband squeeze and turn it that extra centimeter or two for the arrows to finally line up. And by doing that, the silicone gasket gets pinched up a bit at the bottom, it doesn't remain flat - but I opted for this pinched gasket than removing it and then facing excessive leakage. After ALL of that, the blender FINALLY turned on [phew]! As for cleaning it after use, it'll be my husband again unscrewing the canister for me, or I'll continue to just leave it on and fill it up with soapy water for a quick blitz to clean it that way (has worked good enough so far).

I tested blending up a collagen smoothie and it came out smooth, no lumps or chunks, but I only used milk, a little cocoa powder and collagen powder - no frozen fruits or anything like that. When blending fresh or frozen organic fruits, we use a vacuum-blender to minimize oxidation and optimize the nutritional content. So I won't be using this portable blender for that. Now that I'm over the major hump of getting it locked/connected, I'll continue using it to make my collagen smoothies. It also has its own magnetic charging cord that works easily/fine; took a couple of hours to fully charge it.

Overall, the price point isn't outrageous, but after experiencing such challenges with trying to use it (I wanted to throw it out the window from frustration at first), I can't say any price is really 'fair'. It works well if you have the muscle to get this thing screwed on. So, as they say in Italy, buona fortuna (good luck)!

title: Great idea, bad implementation
text: After my immersion blender finally bit the dust, I ordered this hoping it would be a great replacement to keep making my smoothies. The idea is wonderful - an all-in-one to blend everything up and drink the smoothie straight out of, and the blades look really easy to clean, which is what I hate about most blenders. I had such high hopes for this. Well, even fully charged, the blades would turn for about 1.5 seconds and then the lights just turn red for about 8 more seconds while the blades do nothing and then it would shut off. It obviously was not powerful enough to blend what I had in there. There is no way to turn it off and try again - you just have to wait for it to time out. I had to repeat this process over ten times to get it to finally work and start blending. It took two full blends after this to actually blend my smoothie. Once it was blended, switching the bottom was pretty easy. Cleaning the blade would be fairly easy, but you need something like a straw cleaner to get into all the grooves where it screws into the bottom of the cup, because whatever you are blending gets all down into that area. BUT, here is the caveat on cleaning the base. The base has a USB-C charging port, and it does not come with a cover!! I have never had an appliance with a USB-C charging port that needs to be washed and does not come with a cover, lol!! So you have to try to scrub this thing down without getting water into the charging port, and the thing gets *really* messy making a smoothie in it. It's nearly impossible, and for something that is supposed to make life easier, just not worth the extra work. On to drinking out of the cup. It is convenient to just leave the smoothie in the cup and go. However, the tab that you can open does not fold all the way back and every time you take a swig of smoothie the thing hits you in the forehead. So your options are to either be hit in the forehead every time, drink it sideways out of the cup, or just remove the lid. I really wish I had nicer things to say about this setup, but I don't see myself using it again in the future.

In my video I filled the blender with whole blueberries, and coursly chopped banana and strawberries and filled it with milk. This blender does an admirable job with the fruit. It does not handle frozen fruit as well as a conventional blender. I would recommend thawing frozen fruit for a few minutes before starting the blender.

I have also begun using the blender for mixing milk & protein powder. It does a outstanding job at that!

The instructions state that you may tip the blender at a 45 degree angle during operation for better results. The cap is all plastic.

I use a brush to clean the top part and a soapy washcloth to clean the bottom. I do not submerge the bottom in water as this would probably shorten the useful life of the blender.

title: Perfect on the go blender!!
text:
My girlfriend begged me to get one of these blenders. Even though we had a ninja blender, she wanted a portable to make smoothies in. This one fit the bill. After all her begging and pleading, it sat, lonely, on the kitchen counter waiting for her to use it. I bought fresh fruit. I bought frozen fruit. I bought yogurt. At one point i put a slice of turkey and a shot of Fireball in it and attempted to make a "meatball" smoothie, but that was terrible! I have to mention, the blender did a perfect job of liquifying the turkey, it just tasted horrible. Finally, after a thorough cleansing, I concocted the perfect berry smoothie.

What's nifty about this blender? Well, its battery powered (via USB-C cable) for one. It takes very little time to charge it, and i can run through quite a few cycles between charges. The operation is as simple as it gets. It's either on or off.. You have to press and hold the switch to turn it on, but can remove pressure once it's on. This prevents accidental blending while in your gym bag or purse.

I has a screw on, bottle-style cap with a lanyard that you can carry it by. You cannot remove the canister from the blender base unfortunately. If there were an additional cap one could screw on to complete the "blend and go" quest, this thing would be unstoppable. But that's a minor inconvenience.

Cleaning is straight forward, wash it under the faucet and move on. I do not recommend running the blades while under the faucet though, it slings water everywhere (I wanted to check all the blocks, so I gave it a shot). It does seem a little dangerous at that point, so I'd watch your kids with this one when it's wash time.

For the price, this thing is hard to bead. Tiny footprint on the kitchen counter, and it fits just fine in almost any bag. Can't go wrong. I'm happy I got it!

I was able to throw them in there and push the little button at the top and vuala..I have chopped up olives. I put tomatoes in it when I want to stuff them inside of chicken breast. It is very tiny. It is not meant for large amounts of food. When I made my salad with the olives, I had to do it a handful of times... but it was still faster than me cutting each individual Olive in half or in thirds. I also did sun dried tomatoes that were inside of a jar. They were so big and I needed them minced. Worked like a charm. There is nothing fancy about how to wash it. Just get a sponge, put some soap on it and wash it. I have used it for 3 different dinners and still haven't needed to charge it. It's small enough to put in my cabinet next to my seasonings. I don't have to keep it on the counter. Or you can sit it in your dish rack. It's out of the way because it's small. Can you tell, I just really love it. Sometimes there isn't a need for large appliances that sit on your counters and require intricate cleaning..

title: Not bad but there are some limitations
text:
[[VIDEOID:818e435db09bcc10fdb3306c0688457c]] This personal blender is very lightweight and delicate.
No need for batteries. It comes with its own USB cord, but not with a USB plug. But I like the fact that it is rechargeable and it doesn't take long to charge.
The jar capacity is 300 cc max. It is recommended not to overfill it so that the blender has some extra room while processing the ingredients. Also, this is not for hot liquids or big ice cubes that could affect the blades.
The blender is not loud. The engine can perform several blending cycles before it runs out of power.
One thing I do like is the safety mechanism for activating the blades. It will simply not start working unless the jar is tightly attached to it and sealed. The red/blue light signaling will tell you if something is not quite right before you start. This instructions are explained clearly in the User's manual. However, I noticed that I have to hold the blender while the engine is on, because the base does not stick to the counter surface. So, if you activate the power button and leave it alone, the vibration will cause the blender to move, which is not very safe.
The lid for the jar consists of two pieces, one of the pieces is a strainer, this is convenient for avoiding small chunks of fruit while you drink of it, or for pouring my smoothie on another container.
The unit is very easy to clean. I can either disassemble the jar or simply fill the jar with soapy water and turn the machine on. Note: The pieces are not dishwasher safe.
Overall, I like this little blender. Despite all its limitations, I am really enjoying all my custom yogurt and fruit smoothies.

title: Excellent cordless portable blender - better than Blendjet
text:
I didn't know what to expect when I ordered. It could be really nice or horrible. It turned out to be excellent.

Compared to my Blendjet 2.0, it is comparable in function and features. It is bigger in capacity and more masculine design, so this one is mine. My wife uses the Blendjet.

This has all of the safety features one can ever expect or want from a blender. It is easy to line up the jar with the power base. It locks with the magnet, and the magnet also serves as a visual guide when locking. Besides the ring of lights on the base will give you a clear signal so that it is virtually impossible to put the jar on incorrectly. If you either under-tighten or over-tighten, the power base will show the red lights and will not activate the blades unless the jar is properly seated.

One press of the power button gives you a 30-second blend. Usually that is all you need. It also stops when the cycle is over. To pulse, press twice. It is very simple to operate. When it is blending, the ring of lights will also tell you how much battery power is left. Also, the battery life is pretty good. For me, it lasts about ten 30-second cycles. It fully charges in about 3 hours if I recall correctly.

Only issue I had was that it leaked. There is a small 1/4" diameter hold on top of the lid. Now, I realize that there must have been a silicone or rubber seal of some kind that was missing from my unit. I have since used a glue gun to fill that hole permanently so no more leaks. I won't be blending any hot liquids or making soups in this unit, so there is no need for vent hole for steam.

I initially called this my gaudy, chic blender because it would literally light up like a Christmas tree each time I used it. But now, that feature has become endearing to me. I like that the blender interacts with me in a very visual way, which I can't miss. Now, it has become my favorite blender after my Vitamix A3500.

title: So great! Way more powerful than I expected. Fun lights feature!
text:
I love this portable blender so much! It is way better than I imagined. I was expecting the motor to not be as powerful as it is. Especially since I’m used to blending in my Vitamix. I was wrong. This thing is powerful! I have blended protein drinks, smoothies and frappes and it pretty effortlessly blends them. It comes with an ice cube tray to make mini cubes. I use the crushed ice feature on my fridge. It blends frozen fruit well too. The lights feature is neat. When it charges, it has red lights around the whole base for how low the battery is. As it charges, the red lights turn green and when it’s fully charged, they are all green.

When you take off the tumbler “cup” part to clean, the blender senses it isn’t snug and connected properly and blinks all the lights red. When it’s reconnected and locked on properly, they all blink green.

To use blend mode, you just press the power button once and press again to shut it off. To use pulse mode, you double click and it will flash yellow to let you know pulse mode is activated. Then press the button and it will pulse. It resets back to blend mode on its own after sitting a few seconds.

The weight is lighter than I thought also. It’s just a little heavier than an full insulated tumbler of the same size (20oz).

It also comes with a screw on bottom that can be used for turning it into a regular tumbler without the blender base. I haven’t tried it yet.

Not that anyone would try to unscrew it from the base while full of liquid, but I figured I’d throw it out there: DON’T EVER UNSCREW WITH LIQUID IN IT, IT WILL ALL POUR OUT!

I add some dish soap and warm water and turn it on for 10 seconds, pour it out and then remove the tumbler and rinse and dry it.

title: Locks up frequently
text:
I mainly got this for the looks - it reminds me of a hot coffee cup but yet it's a portable blender, yay! Based on its performance though...it's not good.

I use these portable blenders for my Oats Overnight shakes because I need them to be blended smooth so I can drink them through a straw with my clear aligners in. This blender is a neat concept and I think if I used it for fruit and liquid it would work better. Using it for my Oats Overnight shakes it leaves quite a bit unblended 100% of the time. I have to run more than one cycle to get it smoother than it's normally giving me. Is that unblended bit a dealbreaker? No, it's a bit of an annoyance but it's a fine tradeoff instead of having to pull out my giant Ninja blender each time to blend my shake. It's also quite a bit quieter than my Ninja blender so that's also a plus. The dealbreaker is that it locks up frequently and I have to shake it around several times to get it to go.

The portability aspect of these types of blenders is stellar. I've taken it with me on several trips and it's super convenient to be able to just blend my oat shakes while I'm in the car or at the river. This portable blender in particular though is not living up to my expectations.

Overall dissatisfied with this purchase and would not purchase again. The locking up this blender does is too annoying for me to deal with. My other two portable blenders don't lock up so I'd rather use them.

I don't add all of my smoothie ingredients all at once, I do it in batches as I feel it's easier than stuffing the blender full. And not that anyone cares probably but here's my go-to smoothie recipe:
I cut up and freeze half a banana with a quarter cup of blueberries. When I'm ready for my smoothie I just take that out of the freezer and put it in the blender along with one cup of almond milk. Blend. Then I add 2 cut up strawberries and 1/4 of an avocado, blend again. Finally I add a container of the Light and Fit Greek yogurt and blend once more. I pour it into my 20 oz blender bottle because I don't think the drink opening is big enough on the blender cup itself, and a 20 oz blender bottle is the perfect size and has a wide opening. Anyway yeah that's it. I love this blender and wish I'd got it much sooner.

title: Small but Pretty Powerful
text:
At first, I thought this little blender felt flimsy and cheap but since using it a few times I think it is pretty good. Make no mistake, it is not like a Ninja-type blender that can eat through ice and frozen fruit, but so far I have tried carrots, apples, grapes, spinach, and bananas and have had good results.
The first time I used it I put apple, banana, and spinach with almond milk. Every time I pushed the start button it quickly flashed red and stopped - I thought it was defective but then I read the directions more closely and realized not to turn it completely upright when starting. The blender should be held initially at around a 45 degree angle then gradually you can hold it upright. After that, it worked perfectly.
My next drink was a combo of carrots, spinach, orange juice and water - not too good as I didn't let it blend long enough. I took the base off and added a few grapes, yogurt, and almond milk - let it blend again and success.
The advantage of this little blender is it is super convenient. No dragging out a huge appliance. Clean-up is easy as you add water to the cup, attach the base, and blend.
Love the ability to charge the blender. Nice for travel. The blender cups seem small but they each actually hold two cups.
I do think it is a bit pricey. Hopefully, it will last.

title: Impressive Quality
text:
I am impressed by the build quality of this blender. I does not feel cheap at all. In fact, it feels similar to a brand name kitchen appliance. It's made of plastic, but feels solid, and robust. The motor is smooth and strong.
The manual says that it's made from food grade ABS. The power is rated at 80 watts, and the speed is 20k rpm. It doesn't specify battery capacity, but it has plenty of amps to blend fruits. The container holds about 1.5 cups of liquid.
The whole unit is not very big. It stands less than 9 inches tall, and is about 3 inches in diameter.
You can rinse the motor unit under a faucet, but you cannot submerge it under water.
There is a safety mechanism to prevent the blades from spinning unless the top is attached and screwed on tight. Double clicking the power button starts the motor. It will run for 2 minutes, but you can turn it off any time by pressing the power button once.
The manual is in English, Japanese, and Korean. It's not perfect English, but it's fairly easy to understand. It's simple to use. This uses a power only USB-C cable, so you must use the included cable to charge it.
Overall, it's a great blender. It's as powerful as a plug-in appliance, yet it's compact and portable.

title: Ingenious and very handy! (PLEASE SEE EDIT)
text:
I’ve used this everyday since receiving it. I drink a vitamin powder that gives me extra energy. Before I got this product I was simply emptying a scoop full of the powder into a water bottle and shaking it. I was always irritated when I’d see undissolved powder on the sides of the bottle or at the bottom. I began using this and now all the power dissolves and I get the full benefit. Also, the powder is not inexpensive so I’m happy knowing none is going to waste. It’s a very simple and excellent design. The blender is housed in the lid. It requires a charge of at least 4 hours. The charge seems to last for 4-5 uses, then needs to be charged again. Simply add your ingredients into the jug. There are lines indicating where the maximum juice should be filled to and where other ingredients should be filled so that the lid fits and everything is blended well. You simply screw the lid onto the jug, press the button twice and the blender starts. Turn the jug upside down so that the blending mechanism is on the bottom and watch your ingredients become your blended creations. While I haven’t done a smoothie yet, I can imagine this is the perfect product to create great smoothies, milkshakes, and margaritas or other blended drinks. One you’re done blending, turn the jug right side up, unscrew the lid and screw on the included top that has a flip open spout that can be used by itself and can be closed securely or there’s a straw that fits with the spout and makes traveling with your drink very easy. A unique magnetic charging cable with a USB-A connection on the other end is included. Clean up is very easy and quick! I connected the USB-A end to a wall charger and keep it plugged in near where I make my vitamin drink, so that charging is easy. The magnetic charging head is unlike any I’ve seen before, but it has a very strong hold and charges well. I really like this product a lot as it very convenient and easy to use and clean!

EDIT: After using this for about 3 weeks I need to change my review completely. Everything was working well until the end 3rd week. Before that I could get 3 days of use out of 1 charge. Then, very quickly it became 2 days on one charge, then one day, and now it won’t hold a charge at all. This product is not what I thought it was. The battery is shoddy and I certainly expect a product like this to last more 6than 6 weeks and then not work again. DON’T BUY THIS PRODUCT UNTIL THEY VASTLY IMPROVE THEIR BATTERY AND CHARGING SYSTEM. I get angry making my vitamin drinks in the morning and having to use the blender that is no longer a blender and shake it. Also, I was rinsing the jug after drinking a combination of juice and some powered vitamin mix and letting it dry for 3 days then washing it. I noticed after two days, there was mold beginning to grow in small places near the lid. AGAIN, DON’T BUY THIS PRODUCT, IT’S CHEAP AND STOPS WORKING. title: One Awesome Little Blender.
text:
First let me give you my background use for wanting to try out this blender and how it performed. I am a full time care taker for my elderly mother who's condition has gotten to the liquid food stage not being able to do solid foods well. And I have been using a professional model Stick Blender which is pretty powerful to blend up a healthy mixture of eggs, concentrated powered fruits & veggies, liquid mineral, omega 3 oils, etc. for her. The blender worked well but had to be well controlled not to make a mess. It was hard to clean along with the big tall container, and had to be used several times to keep the mixture over time as drank over a period of time by her. So I was open to another solution as my normal big heavy countertop blender quit working some time back.

I was very skeptical about this battery powered little blender when I first came across it. But I thought it would be worth a try plus it was just the right size. Not only did it do a great job for what I wanted it to do, it did much more without having to carry back and forth a big glass mix container to countertop base if going the standard blender route. I could put all the ingredients in and blend, then pour into my mom’s cup what she would drink in a limited time period and just keep the rest in the blender until ready again. Then where she was at, just a click of the power button to remix all that settled or separated inside and then pour some more into her cup. When all done, clean up was much faster, easier, and less messy with a couple drops of liquid soap in the top hole, hot water, blend, and pour out. I found for final rinse, with top off and 3/4 full off hot water with the blender in the sink pointed at 45 degree angle under the faucets running water and YOUR HAND OVER THE TOP to keep the water exploding outwards, you can hit the start button and it would mix with some coming out while the faucet kept putting more in to rinse completely after you then removed your hand. That is much easier than the stick mixer and container, or big old counter top mixer.

The simple screw on lid with snap open/close part to seal during mixing, or open to pour is real handy. The solid lid for travel/storage is nice too.

The only real problem I ran across was detaching the base from mixing column. The clear mixer container with bottom centered magnet to ensure closed position can close so tightly it can be next to impossible to untwist open again. To fix that, I had to order from Amazon some Food Grade Silicone Oil. The maker of this should have included some this for the rubber seal at the bottom and the plastic treads. That was an extra $10 dollars but is enough to use on everything with seals you own. > https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B09JYXMBLK/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1

This blender is rechargeable with nice lights to let you know how much the power level is down, and what your recharge progress is. All in all, this is a great little blender for home use or travel all at a reasonable sell price.

title: Capacity is clearly not even 16oz - I measured it
text:
The capacity of this blender is not the largest portable blender. Not by a long shot.

I poured a 16oz bottle of water into the blender and it overflowed -- meaning that the capacity on this thing is not even 16oz.

I then poured the same 16oz bottle of water into a Blendjet 2 and it fit perfectly.

The markings on the bottle also go up to 400ml (13.5oz - see photo). I'd say the max capacity is around 14oz.

I posted a question regarding this, and the answerer claims that they measured it. So I measured it myself, and it's not even 16oz. It's very disappointing.

PLEASE also note that if you fill it up too high, even with just Water, you'll get a "EL" error, and you won't spin (no info about this on their website), but I've gathered that it means it's filled up too high, because removing some water helped after that.

Overall, if you're trying to blend smoothies, you need that extra 2-4oz that they CLAIM you have, here. Unfortunately, you don't. It's a 14-15oz blender that claims 17.5oz and you can only fill it up to about 12oz without an error.

Blendi needs to release a larger capacity cup, because this is false advertising.

title: Pretty good, not great...
text:
Overall it's pretty decent for the price. Definitely convenient, but my typical protein shake (2 scoops powder, half banana, few frozen strawberries, 4-5 ice cubes and 10oz almond milk) caused the blender to bind up. Had to hold it upside down for a few seconds to get it going again, which it did. Didn't chop the ice cubes totally, instead leaving them in chunks a few centimeters big. It did mix the frozen strawberries ok. Cleaning was easy.

Few things I don't like:
-The strap attached to the lid is useless. I think the manufacturer intends someone to clip this entire thing to their belt and walk around with it. That is ridiculous as it's way too heavy fully assembled. If it included a 2nd lid that would fit the bottom, then maybe that could work. Otherwise any liquid in the cup will just spill out anytime the strap is used.
-The cup has a little black magnet glued into it which is used as a safety feature. When you tighten the cup onto the base, the magnet aligns with a certain spot in the base allowing the mixer to operate. If you don't have it aligned perfectly, it won't turn on. I can definitely see that little magnet falling out at some point, probably into the drink or someone's mouth. Plus it's on the end of the cup you drink out of, unless you drink with the cup still attached to the base, which more and more I am thinking that's how it was intended. Don't like that.
-My biggest complaint is the lid, because is not flat. It is convex so you cant really set the cup portion down. So unless you're going to slam your entire shake at once or take the entire mixer with you, you'll either have to hold it the entire time or transfer it to another container. The lid thing is dumb, should definitely be flat and have a 2nd lid for the other side.

title: cute, practical and i use it almost every week!
text:
you have to plug it in over night even if it says it's ¨fully charged¨ after one use its most likely not because it takes a while for it to blend, but once it blends man it blends. Its a really good mini blender, i got it to replace my stupid hand blender (or whatever you call the microthingie) Because i needed something that well...well blend (duh) and its good....I dont want to give it 5 stars and i almost gave it three stars because if your an impairment person (im assuming most of you are because who has the time with a big blender that takes over the counter am i right?) This takes up no space at all and works great on frozen stuff but if your trying to do frozen pinapple make sure you shake it.

I will give it props for you not needing to hold the on button the whole time you use it. Once you figure out how to ¨turn it on¨ it works like a dream. You have to coax it sometimes like shake it once and it will work. (ive heard others have this problem too so its not just me)

and the charge cable is something you have to get used to. I dont know why they give you such a tinny cable for something that needs to be plugged in ALOT but thats just me. I wonder what would happen if i plugged in one of my USB-C cables...

Its great with any kind of milk and if you want a smoothie or a milk then by all means this is your go to thing. DO NOT PUT IT IN THE DISH WASHER! I have not been able to figure out how to clean it the ¨proper way¨ but if you've had a small blender and know how to clean them then i'm sure you'll be ok with it.

You will see there's a black arrow pointing down on it. You have to match the arrow with the seem looking thing on the side of the cup in order for it to turn on. Im sure its some kind of safty measure thing because ive tried to turn it on with the blender not connected and even though it has power it wont turn on, so that makes it safe for kids if your looking for something for their back to school smoothies. Just note that you MUST charge it every night before bed to be safe. I think i got two uses out of it once, but yea. Its also kinda loud. Not loud loud, but loud enough.

I have not tried making a frappichino in it, so i dont know if it can do that. i want to, but im kinda nervous. I got it for prime day and it came a few days later. So yea. I also got it for a steller price too i dono what the price is now for it, but its a wonderful little gizmo. I got it cause i needed a blender that didn't take up all my upper body strength for the day and this one is just a couple pushes and shakes and bam instant smoothy!

If your looking for something bigger this bad boy might not be for you, but its the perfect size and can make up to 8-10 ozs which is perfect for me because i usually waste what i make in the stupid hand blender.

I also haven't tried a frozen banana in it yet, but if it can take frozen peaches and mangos then im sure it can take a banana or two. (half a banana)

title: Love for travel and having it on the road. Super convenient.
text:
I purchased this wonders since I travel a lot. I try to eat healthy and keep my protein intake out on the road. This blender was perfect for that.
I mainly use it for protein shakes. Yes, you can shake them up, but it’s so much better running them through a blender, and now I’m able to do that even on the road. I also love that I’m able to pack it up in my suitcase, and it does not take up much space whatsoever. You don’t even have to plug it in because you can just throw in some batteries. However, if you want to plug it in, there is a USB that you can use.
The cleaning is super easy. I love cleaning blenders like this. You basically just throw in some water, soap, and push the button. Rinse out and it’s clean. Super super easy.
